q: A security team just disabled a Microsoft Entra ID account after confirming its credentials were compromised, but the attacker still has an already-issued access token that would otherwise remain valid for up to another hour. What should be enabled so relying services revoke that token immediately instead of waiting for it to expire?
opts: A stricter Conditional Access sign-in frequency setting
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE)
A shorter static access token lifetime policy
Microsoft Entra ID Protection user risk remediation
why: Continuous Access Evaluation pushes critical events, like an account being disabled, directly to CAE-enabled relying services in near real time, revoking the token immediately rather than waiting for its natural expiration. A shorter static token lifetime only narrows the exposure window in advance, it does not react to this specific event after the fact, and sign-in frequency and ID Protection risk remediation govern future sign-ins, not an already-issued token.

q: Contoso must block sign-ins to its Finance app from one specific country and require a compliant device for sign-ins from every other location. The requirements apply only to members of the Finance group. Which configuration should you use?
opts: One Conditional Access policy for the Finance group that selects both Block access and Require device to be marked as compliant for the country
Two Conditional Access policies scoped to the Finance group and the app: one blocks the country's named location, the other requires a compliant device
A named location for the country marked as trusted, plus an Entra ID Protection sign-in risk policy that blocks high-risk sign-ins
An authentication strength that requires phishing-resistant MFA for the Finance group, applied to the Finance app
why: Block access is a standalone grant that cannot be combined with other grant controls in the same policy, so the block and the compliant-device requirement need separate policies, each scoped to the Finance group and app. Marking a location trusted never blocks anything, and a sign-in risk policy reacts to risk signals rather than a specific country. An authentication strength changes which MFA methods are accepted; it neither restricts the sign-in country nor checks device compliance.

q: An Azure Function must read secrets from a Key Vault that uses the Azure RBAC permission model. No credentials may be stored in code or app settings, and the Function must receive only the permissions it needs. What should you do?
opts: Create an app registration and store its client secret as a Key Vault-referenced app setting
Give a user-assigned identity the Key Vault Administrator role at subscription scope so future vaults also work
Enable a system-assigned identity on the Function and assign it Key Vault Contributor on the vault
Enable a system-assigned identity on the Function and assign it Key Vault Secrets User on the vault
why: A managed identity removes stored credentials entirely, and Key Vault Secrets User at vault scope grants only the data-plane read of secret values the Function needs. Key Vault Contributor is a management-plane role: it lets you manage the vault resource but does not grant access to secret values. Administrator at subscription scope violates least privilege, and an app registration secret is still a credential that has to live somewhere, even when it is referenced through a Key Vault-backed setting.

q: Contoso's Global Administrator must grant an auditor the Reader role on an Azure subscription, but the administrator has no Azure RBAC role on that subscription. What should the administrator do first?
opts: Activate the Privileged Role Administrator role in PIM, then assign the Azure role from the Entra roles page
Enable Access management for Azure resources, which grants User Access Administrator at root scope, then create the role assignment
Assign the Owner role on the subscription from the Entra admin center's Roles and administrators page
Create a custom Entra role that includes Azure role assignment write actions and assign it to the administrator
why: Entra directory roles and Azure RBAC roles are separate authorization systems, so Global Administrator does not itself carry Azure permissions. The elevation toggle in Entra properties grants User Access Administrator at the root scope, which allows the role assignment (and should be removed afterwards). Privileged Role Administrator only manages Entra role assignments, the Entra roles page does not assign Azure roles, and custom Entra roles cover directory actions, not Azure resource actions.

q: Fabrikam guest users must request a group, a SharePoint site, and an app from Contoso through one approval workflow. Access must expire automatically after 90 days, with minimal administrative effort. Which should you create?
opts: A Microsoft 365 group that is granted all three resources, with a group expiration policy of 90 days
PIM for Groups with the guests as eligible members of a group that is granted all three resources
An access package with a request policy for the partner's connected organization and a 90-day expiration
A dynamic group for the partner's guests, with an access review that removes members after 90 days
why: An access package bundles several resources behind one request-and-approval policy and ends each assignment automatically on its expiration date. A group expiration policy expires the group itself, not individual users' access. PIM for Groups requires an administrator to grant eligibility and offers no self-service request for external users. A dynamic group has no request or approval step, and an access review checks access users already hold rather than granting it.

q: A Contoso user's account is compromised while the user is working in an application that supports Continuous Access Evaluation. Which two events are CAE critical events that revoke the user's existing access token in near real time? (Choose two.)
opts: An administrator explicitly revokes all refresh tokens for the user
The user's job title is changed in the directory
Entra ID Protection raises the user's risk level to high
The user's license assignment is changed
A Conditional Access policy is created in report-only mode
why: CAE critical events include an account being disabled or deleted, a password change or reset, MFA being enabled for the user, an administrator revoking all refresh tokens, and Entra ID Protection detecting high user risk. Attribute edits such as a job title, a license change, or creating a report-only Conditional Access policy are not critical events, so the existing token keeps working until it expires.

q: Fabrikam users sign in to a Contoso app with their own Entra credentials. Contoso wants to avoid a second MFA prompt for Fabrikam users who already completed MFA in their home tenant, and for no other partner. What should you configure?
opts: The default cross-tenant access inbound trust setting that accepts MFA claims from every external tenant
Cross-tenant synchronization that provisions Fabrikam users as members of Contoso's tenant
A connected organization for Fabrikam in entitlement management, with a policy that requires MFA
An organization-specific inbound trust setting for Fabrikam that accepts its MFA claims
why: Cross-tenant access settings let you add an organization-specific entry for Fabrikam and trust only its MFA claims for inbound B2B sign-ins. Changing the default setting would extend that trust to every external tenant. Cross-tenant synchronization provisions accounts but does not decide whether MFA claims are trusted, and a connected organization in entitlement management scopes who can request access packages rather than how sign-in claims are treated.

q: Microsoft Entra PIM can require approval and justification when a user activates an eligible assignment for a Microsoft Entra directory role, but those activation requirements are not available for Azure resource roles such as Owner or Contributor.
opts: True
False
why: PIM applies the same eligible/active model, and the same role settings (justification, approval, MFA, maximum duration), to Azure resource roles and to Entra directory roles. Treating Azure RBAC roles as a weaker, standing-access category is a common misconception.

q: An administrator who turns on Access management for Azure resources becomes Owner of every Azure subscription in the tenant.
opts: True
False
why: The elevation grants User Access Administrator at the root scope, which lets the administrator assign Azure roles (including Owner) but is not Owner itself. Global Administrator alone grants no Azure role, and the elevation should be removed once the assignment work is done.

q: A user-assigned managed identity is deleted automatically when the last Azure resource it is attached to is deleted.
opts: True
False
why: A user-assigned managed identity is its own resource and persists, along with its role assignments, until someone deletes it. It is a system-assigned identity whose lifecycle is tied to its single resource.

q: For an application that supports Continuous Access Evaluation, Microsoft Entra ID may issue access tokens with a lifetime much longer than the usual default, because revoking access no longer depends on the token expiring.
opts: True
False
why: CAE-capable clients can receive longer-lived tokens precisely because critical events such as account disablement or token revocation are pushed to the service in near real time. It sounds like a weakening, but the revocation path is event-driven rather than expiry-driven.

q: Contoso is designing a single Conditional Access policy for a SaaS app. Which two configurations are valid in that policy? (Choose two.)
opts: Block access and Require MFA selected together, so access is blocked only if MFA fails
A location condition that includes a country or region
Require device to be marked as compliant or Require MFA, using Require one of the selected controls
A condition that evaluates inbound TCP port 3389 on the VM that hosts the app
An assignment scope of an Azure resource group so the policy applies to the resources inside
why: Conditional Access conditions include user or group, application, location (including countries or regions) and device platform, and grant controls can be combined with AND or OR logic. Block access is exclusive and cannot be paired with other grant controls. Port-level traffic is an NSG or firewall concern, and Conditional Access targets users, workload identities and cloud apps, not Azure resource groups.

q: Contoso's GitHub Actions workflow deploys to Azure, and Fabrikam employees use a Contoso app after signing in with their own tenant. Which two designs are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: Store a client secret in GitHub secrets and rotate it quarterly, because federation still requires a secret
Use workload identity federation so Fabrikam employees can sign in to the Contoso app without MFA
Configure cross-tenant access settings to trust Fabrikam's MFA claims for inbound B2B sign-ins
Configure a federated identity credential that trusts the GitHub token issuer and the repository subject
Configure cross-tenant synchronization so the GitHub Actions workflow can obtain Entra tokens
why: A federated identity credential lets the workflow exchange its GitHub token for an Entra token with no stored secret, and cross-tenant access settings are where trust in a partner's MFA claims is set for human B2B sign-ins. Federation exists to remove the secret, it is for non-human workloads rather than partner employees, and cross-tenant synchronization provisions user accounts, not workload tokens.

q: An engineer needs the Contributor role on a production resource group only while deploying. Contoso requires that every use of the role be justified and approved by a manager, and that the engineer hold no permissions at other times. What should you configure in PIM?
opts: An active assignment with an end date, so the role is available only during the deployment window
A permanent active assignment, with a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for the Azure portal
An eligible assignment, with activation limited to 24 hours and no further requirements
An eligible assignment, with the role setting requiring justification and approval at activation
why: An eligible assignment means no permissions until the engineer activates, and the role setting is where approval and justification are enforced. A time-bound active assignment grants the role for the whole window with no per-use approval. A permanent active assignment is standing access whatever Conditional Access adds, and an eligible assignment without approval meets the no-standing-access goal but not the manager-approval requirement.

q: Guest users must request a bundle of resources through one approval flow with automatic expiration. A resource owner must also periodically re-certify access that is still active. Which combination should you use?
opts: A dynamic group for guest users, with a Conditional Access policy requiring periodic re-authentication
An access package for the request flow, with an access review scoped to that package's assignments
PIM for Groups with eligible membership, with quarterly notifications sent to the resource owner
An access package for the request flow, with a leaver lifecycle workflow to re-certify access
why: The access package supplies the bundled request, approval and expiration, and an access review attached to its assignments is the recurring owner re-certification. A dynamic group has no request flow and re-authentication does not ask anyone whether access should continue. PIM for Groups notifications are not a certification decision, and lifecycle workflows run joiner, mover and leaver tasks from HR-style triggers rather than collecting owner attestations.

q: A resource owner must re-certify guest users' membership in a group every 90 days. If the owner does not respond, the guests' access must be removed without administrator action. What should you configure?
opts: An access package assignment for each guest that expires after 90 days, with no further configuration
An access review of the group, recurring every 90 days, with the no-response action set to take no action
An access review of the group with the owner as reviewer, recurring every 90 days, with the no-response action set to remove access
A Microsoft 365 group expiration policy of 90 days, with the owner renewing the group when notified
why: An access review is the recurring re-certification of access already held, and its default decision for non-responders controls what happens when the owner is silent, so remove access is the setting that meets the requirement. The same review with a take-no-action default would leave unreviewed guests in place. An assignment expiry is a one-time cutoff rather than a recurring review, and a group expiration policy renews or deletes the whole group instead of individual guest memberships.

q: HR records an employee's last day in an attribute synced to Microsoft Entra ID. Contoso wants the account disabled and group memberships removed on that date without an administrator performing those steps. What should you configure?
opts: An entitlement management access package assigned to the employee and set to expire on the leave date
A Conditional Access policy that blocks sign-in for users whose leave-date attribute has passed
A recurring access review of all groups, with auto-apply enabled and non-responding users removed
A leaver lifecycle workflow scheduled from the employee leave date, with disable-account and remove-from-groups tasks
why: Lifecycle workflows run a set of tasks, including disabling the account and removing group memberships, automatically relative to an HR attribute such as the leave date. An expiring access package removes only access granted through that package and leaves the account enabled. Conditional Access cannot evaluate a custom date attribute and would not remove memberships, and an access review is a periodic attestation that is not tied to a person's leave date.

q: Contoso is about to enable a Conditional Access policy that requires compliant devices for all administrators. Contoso wants to be certain that a misconfiguration cannot lock every administrator out of the tenant. Which account design should already exist?
opts: A federated account synced from on-premises AD, with permanent Global Administrator and MFA required through Conditional Access
A cloud-only account holding a PIM-eligible Global Administrator assignment, covered by the compliant-device policy
Two cloud-only accounts with permanent Global Administrator, excluded from Conditional Access policies and monitored for sign-ins
A partner guest account with a permanent Global Administrator role, excluded from every Conditional Access policy
why: Emergency access accounts must be cloud-only, permanently assigned, independent of the policies that could fail, and monitored because any use is an exceptional event. A federated synced account depends on on-premises infrastructure and is still subject to the policy. A PIM-eligible account needs a working sign-in and activation path, and a policy that covers it would block it too. A guest account relies on another tenant, which makes it unsuitable as the last resort.

q: Conditional Access authentication context lets a policy require phishing-resistant MFA specifically at the moment a user activates a privileged role through PIM, rather than only at initial sign-in.
opts: True
False
why: Authentication context tags a specific sensitive action, like PIM role activation, so a Conditional Access policy can require a stronger control exactly at that moment instead of treating every sign-in and every later privileged action identically.

q: Contoso is choosing between Password Hash Synchronization and Pass-through Authentication for its hybrid identities. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Password hash synchronization sends the plaintext password to Entra ID for validation at each sign-in
Pass-through Authentication keeps a password hash in Entra ID so sign-ins work with no on-premises connectivity
Password hash synchronization lets cloud sign-ins continue when all on-premises domain controllers are offline
Pass-through Authentication validates the password against on-premises AD, so sign-in fails if no agent can reach a domain controller
Entra Connect Health must be configured before either method can be used
why: With password hash sync, Entra ID validates against a synchronized hash, so cloud sign-ins do not depend on on-premises availability. Pass-through Authentication validates in real time against AD through its agents, so it needs connectivity to a domain controller. The plaintext password is never sent for validation under hash sync, Pass-through Authentication does not store a hash, and Connect Health is optional monitoring.

q: Contoso configures two Conditional Access policies that use Entra ID Protection signals: one for sign-in risk and one for user risk. Which grant controls match the intended remediation for each, with the least disruption to legitimate users?
opts: Sign-in risk: require a secure password change. User risk: require MFA for that session
Sign-in risk: block access for the account. User risk: require MFA for that session
Sign-in risk: require MFA for that session. User risk: require a secure password change
Both policies: block access until an administrator manually dismisses the risk
why: A risky sign-in is a single event, so an MFA challenge lets the legitimate user prove themselves for that session. A risky user means the credential itself may be compromised, so a secure password change is the remediation that actually fixes it. Swapping them applies a session-level control to a compromised credential, and password-change requirements to a one-off event. Blocking everything works but causes the disruption the question asks you to avoid.

q: Contoso users keep choosing passwords such as 'C0ntoso!2024', built from the company name with common character substitutions. Contoso wants these rejected when users set a password. What should you configure?
opts: Lower the smart lockout threshold so repeated guesses of such passwords lock the account sooner
Add the company and product names to the custom banned password list in Microsoft Entra Password Protection
Increase the minimum password length for cloud users to 14 characters
Shorten the password expiration period so predictable passwords are replaced quickly
why: A custom banned password list adds organization-specific terms to the global list, and Password Protection also normalizes common character substitutions, so variants of the company name are rejected at change time. Smart lockout slows guessing at sign-in and does not govern which password can be set. Longer minimum length and shorter expiry still allow a long or recently set password that contains the company name.

q: Contoso protects PIM role activation with a Conditional Access authentication context. A review found that SMS codes can be relayed through a real-time phishing proxy. Which requirement ensures activation can use only methods that resist this attack?
opts: The built-in Multifactor authentication strength
The built-in Passwordless MFA authentication strength
The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength
A compliant device and a trusted named location for PIM activation
why: The Phishing-resistant MFA strength limits sign-in to methods such as FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication, which are bound to the site and cannot be relayed. The Multifactor strength still accepts SMS and push, and the Passwordless strength also allows the Authenticator phone sign-in method, which is not classed as phishing-resistant. Device and location conditions do not change which authentication method is accepted.

q: Contoso wants IT staff in one regional office to act as Helpdesk Administrators only for users in that region, not for the whole tenant. Which configuration achieves this?
opts: Create a security group of the regional IT staff and assign Helpdesk Administrator to that group at directory scope
Assign Helpdesk Administrator through PIM with a maximum activation duration of eight hours
Create an administrative unit that contains the regional users and assign Helpdesk Administrator scoped to that unit
Create a custom role limited to password reset and assign it at directory scope to the regional IT staff
why: An administrative unit limits where a directory role applies, so the assignment covers only the users in the unit. A group assignment, a PIM time limit and a narrower custom role all change who holds the role, how long, or what actions it contains, but each still applies to every user at directory scope. Scope is the axis that matters here, and only the administrative unit changes it.

q: A nightly batch job authenticates unattended as a single-tenant service principal using a certificate. Security wants that service principal to authenticate only from the company's egress IP range. What should you configure?
opts: A user-targeted Conditional Access policy applied to the app's owners and restricted to the egress named location
A federated identity credential on the app registration with a subject claim limited to the batch host
A Conditional Access policy that targets the service principal and blocks sign-ins from outside the egress named location
A certificate policy on the app registration that limits the certificate's validity to 90 days
why: Conditional Access for workload identities can target a single-tenant service principal and evaluate a named location condition before it is allowed to authenticate. A user-targeted policy applies to people, not to the service principal the job signs in as. A federated credential replaces the certificate with a trust relationship but does not restrict source IP, and shorter certificate validity limits exposure time rather than where sign-ins originate.

q: An operations team must rotate client secrets and certificates on all app registrations, but must not be able to change redirect URIs, API permissions or owners. The built-in application roles allow those changes. What should you do?
opts: Assign the Application Administrator role through PIM with a short activation window
Assign the Application Developer role so the team can manage credentials on apps they did not create
Make each team member an owner of every app registration
Create a custom Entra role with only the app credentials update permission and assign it to the team
why: A custom role can contain exactly one permission, here updating application credentials, and nothing else. Application Administrator through PIM is time-limited but still allows editing redirect URIs, permissions and owners. Application Developer does not extend to apps the user does not own, and ownership of an app registration lets the owner edit every property of that app.

q: Marking a named location as 'trusted' in Conditional Access only affects which IP ranges are grouped under that name, with no effect on how Microsoft Entra ID Protection evaluates a sign-in's risk level.
opts: True
False
why: Trusted named locations are also factored into Identity Protection's own risk evaluation, with sign-ins from a trusted location weighted as lower risk — a named location that is never marked trusted does not get that same weighting.

q: Cross-tenant synchronization automatically creates, updates, and removes user accounts in a target tenant, while cross-tenant access settings alone only govern how much an already-existing B2B sign-in is trusted, without provisioning any accounts.
opts: True
False
why: Cross-tenant synchronization is the provisioning mechanism, commonly used across subsidiaries under one organization, while cross-tenant access settings adjust trust (MFA and device claims) for a sign-in from an account that must already exist — the two solve different parts of a multi-tenant relationship.

q: Contoso wants engineers to receive time-bound membership of a group that is assigned the Contributor role on a subscription. Which two statements about using PIM for Groups are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Eligible members activate their membership or ownership, and activation can require justification and approval
PIM for Groups works only for groups that are assigned Entra directory roles
Activation of eligible membership requires the user to hold the Global Administrator role
Membership activated through PIM for Groups cannot have an end time and stays until removed manually
A group assigned an Azure RBAC role gives its members that role while their membership is active
why: PIM for Groups applies the eligible/active, time-bound model to membership and ownership, with the same justification and approval options as role activation, and a group that holds an Azure role passes it to members for as long as their membership is active. It is not limited to groups with Entra roles, needs no special role to activate, and activations are time-bound by design.

q: Contoso's users keep granting a third-party calendar app access to their mailboxes. The security team wants users to consent only to apps from verified publishers with low-impact permissions, and wants everything else routed to reviewers instead of blocking users outright. What should be configured?
opts: User consent disabled completely for the tenant, so only administrators can ever grant app permissions
A weekly access review of every enterprise application assigned to users in the tenant
User consent limited to verified publishers for selected permissions, plus the admin consent workflow with designated reviewers
A Conditional Access policy that blocks sign-in to all apps that Contoso has not registered in its tenant
why: Limiting user consent to verified publishers with selected low-impact permissions and enabling the admin consent workflow lets users request anything beyond that, which reviewers can approve or deny. Disabling consent entirely leaves users stuck, since the requirement is routing requests to reviewers. Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions rather than OAuth grants, and weekly access reviews of apps are slow and do not prevent the initial consent.

q: An app registration has the application permission Files.ReadWrite.All granted with admin consent, and no user ever signs in to it. A reviewer asks what that grant means. Which description is correct?
opts: The app can read and write only the files of the one user who originally consented to it
The permission only applies to files that have been shared with the app's registered owner
The app can read and write all files as itself, without a signed-in user
The permission is ignored unless a user signs in to the app and approves the request
why: Application permissions let an app act as itself with no user present, so Files.ReadWrite.All gives tenant-wide file access and always needs administrator consent. A delegated permission would be limited by the signed-in user's own access. The grant does not depend on user sign-in, and it is not limited to the owner's files.

q: A Key Vault firewall that allows only a selected virtual network also gives users in that network permission to read the vault's secrets.
opts: True
False
why: Network access and authorization are separate controls. The firewall only decides who may reach the vault endpoint, and callers still need data-plane permissions through Azure RBAC or access policies to read secrets.

q: A certificate stored in Key Vault was issued by an integrated certificate authority and expired last month, causing an outage. Which setting prevents a repeat without manual work?
opts: A lifecycle action on the certificate policy that auto-renews it before expiry
A soft-delete retention period of 90 days for every key and secret in the vault
Purge protection on the vault with the maximum retention period
A CanNotDelete resource lock on the vault and its resource group
why: Certificate policies in Key Vault support lifecycle actions that renew automatically at a set point before expiry when using an integrated CA, which removes the manual step. A resource lock stops deletion of the resource, and purge protection and soft-delete retention protect against deleted objects, not against certificates expiring.

q: Contoso wants to know which VMs and deployment resources in Azure, AWS and Google Cloud contain exposed passwords and connection strings, without installing anything on the machines. Which capability does that?
opts: Defender for Key Vault alerts
Azure Policy audit of Key Vault configuration
Defender CSPM secrets scanning, including agentless scanning of VM disks
File integrity monitoring on each VM
why: Defender CSPM provides agentless secrets scanning of multicloud VMs and infrastructure-as-code deployment resources, and surfaces findings in recommendations, security explorer and attack paths. Defender for Key Vault detects suspicious vault access rather than secrets stored elsewhere, a Key Vault Azure Policy checks vault settings, and file integrity monitoring tracks file changes and needs an agent.

q: An attacker with a stolen administrator credential could disable soft delete and delete Contoso's Azure Backup data. Which feature requires a second approver before such protected operations can happen?
opts: Multi-user authorization using a Resource Guard in a separate subscription
Soft delete with the default 14-day retention that applies to every deleted backup item
The Backup Reader role assigned to every administrator who manages the vault
Encryption of the vault with customer-managed keys stored in a separate Key Vault
why: Multi-user authorization places protected operations behind a Resource Guard whose administrators must approve them, ideally owned by a different team or subscription. Backup Reader is read-only but does not add an approval step, soft delete only retains deleted data, and customer-managed keys control encryption rather than who can disable protections.

q: Operations staff must run restores from Azure Backup but must not be able to delete backups or change policies. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: The Backup Operator role fits, because it excludes removing backups and managing policies
Backup Reader can run restores and change retention
Soft delete keeps deleted backup data for 14 additional days at no extra cost
Backup Contributor fits, because it cannot create or manage backups
why: Backup Operator can do what Contributor does except removing backups and managing policies, which matches the requirement, and soft delete adds a 14-day safety net for deleted backup data. Backup Contributor can create and manage backups, and Backup Reader is view-only.

q: Defender for Cloud reports that several service principals and guest accounts hold Contributor on production subscriptions but have not used the access in 90 days. Which feature identifies and recommends right-sizing this access across clouds?
opts: Azure Policy with the Audit effect applied to role assignments at subscription scope
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, which analyzes permissions across clouds
Cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) in the Defender CSPM plan
Network Watcher effective security rules on each network interface
why: CIEM in Defender CSPM analyzes effective permissions, flags inactive or overprovisioned identities and recommends removing or narrowing access across Azure, AWS and GCP. Microsoft Entra Permissions Management is deprecated, Azure Policy evaluates resource configuration rather than identity usage, and Network Watcher deals with traffic rules.

q: Contoso needs a role that can read VM configuration and start or stop VMs but nothing else, and no built-in role fits. Where must the custom Azure role be assignable?
opts: Only at the tenant root, regardless of what the definition says
Only at the management group that defines the policy initiative
Only to users, never to groups or service principals
At the scopes listed in its AssignableScopes, such as a subscription or resource group
why: AssignableScopes in the role definition decide where it can be assigned, such as a management group, subscription or resource group, and the role can then be given to users, groups and service principals. It is not limited to the tenant root or to users, and policy initiatives have no bearing on role assignability.

q: A team deploys Bicep templates that keep creating storage accounts with public network access enabled. Contoso wants the mistake caught in pull requests and also blocked if it still reaches deployment. Which combination meets both needs?
opts: Defender for Storage enabled on every subscription that hosts the storage accounts
A ReadOnly resource lock on every resource group that holds storage accounts
Weekly access reviews of the service connection that the pipeline uses to deploy
Defender for Cloud DevOps security IaC scanning in the pipeline, plus an Azure Policy deny assignment for public access
why: IaC scanning reports misconfigurations at pull request time, and an Azure Policy with a deny effect is the backstop that blocks a non-compliant deployment. Resource locks protect resources from deletion or modification but do not validate configuration, access reviews do not inspect templates, and Defender for Storage detects threats after deployment.

q: Contoso wants a single dashboard that compares its Azure resources with ISO 27001 and also with its own internal security rules. What should it do in Defender for Cloud?
opts: Replace the Microsoft cloud security benchmark with ISO 27001 and drop every other standard
Disable all recommendations and track compliance in a spreadsheet instead
Create a Sentinel workbook for each standard and chart the incidents by hand
Add the ISO 27001 standard and create a custom standard for the internal rules
why: Defender for Cloud lets admins add regulatory standards and create custom standards, and both appear in the regulatory compliance view. A Sentinel workbook would not assess resources, the benchmark is the default baseline and need not be replaced, and a spreadsheet is not an assessment.

q: Applications that require user assignment can always be consented by users, as long as user consent is allowed for the tenant.
opts: True
False
why: Apps that require users to be assigned must have their permissions consented by an administrator, even when user consent policies would otherwise let users consent for themselves.

q: A hub VNet routes outbound traffic from all spokes through Azure Firewall. Security must detect known exploit signatures inside outbound HTTPS requests, without deploying additional appliances. What should you do?
opts: Use Azure Firewall Standard with threat intelligence set to Alert and deny
Deploy Application Gateway WAF_v2 in Prevention mode in the hub VNet
Use Azure Firewall Premium with TLS inspection and IDPS enabled in its policy
Use Azure Firewall Standard with application rules that reference FQDN tags
why: Matching signatures inside HTTPS payloads needs a firewall that can decrypt traffic (TLS inspection) and run intrusion detection and prevention, which are Azure Firewall Premium capabilities and need no extra appliance. Standard threat intelligence and FQDN tags filter by destination reputation or name, not payload content. A WAF protects inbound web applications, not outbound traffic from spokes.

q: Administrators must connect to Windows and Linux VMs over RDP and SSH directly from a browser session in the Azure portal. The VMs have no public IP addresses, no inbound RDP or SSH may be open from the internet, and no VPN client software may be installed. What should you deploy?
opts: A point-to-site VPN gateway so administrators reach the VMs by private IP address
Just-in-time VM access, requesting port 3389 and 22 from the administrators' source IPs
An Azure Firewall DNAT rule that publishes RDP and SSH from the firewall's public IP
Azure Bastion in an AzureBastionSubnet of the VNet, with connections made through the portal
why: Azure Bastion proxies RDP and SSH over TLS from the portal to VMs that have only private IPs, so nothing is published to the internet and no client is needed. A point-to-site VPN needs client software and is not portal-based. JIT access still opens a management port on a reachable IP for a time window, and a DNAT rule publishes the ports on the firewall's public IP, which is exactly the exposure being avoided.

q: Azure VMs and on-premises servers connected over ExpressRoute private peering must reach an Azure SQL Database through private IP addresses, with public network access disabled. What should you configure?
opts: A service endpoint for Microsoft.Sql on the VM subnets, with virtual network rules on the server
A private endpoint for the SQL server in a VNet both networks can reach, then disable public network access
ExpressRoute Microsoft peering with a route filter for Azure SQL, plus an NSG that blocks internet traffic
An NSG rule using the Sql service tag on the VM subnets, plus a server firewall rule for the on-premises range
why: A private endpoint places a private IP for the server in the VNet, reachable from Azure and from on-premises over the circuit's private peering, and it is what allows public network access to be disabled. A service endpoint keeps the public endpoint and is not reachable from on-premises. Microsoft peering and service-tag rules still reach the server's public IP addresses, so the public endpoint stays in use.

q: Contoso publishes a global web app through Azure Front Door. Security must block SQL injection attempts at the edge, before traffic reaches the origin, with minimal ongoing effort. What should you do?
opts: Associate a WAF policy that uses the Default Rule Set in Prevention mode with the Front Door endpoint
Deploy Application Gateway WAF_v2 in each origin region and keep Front Door for caching only
Deploy Azure Firewall Premium with IDPS in each origin VNet, in Alert and deny mode
Enable DDoS Protection on the origin's public IP address and set a mitigation threshold
why: A Front Door WAF policy with a managed rule set in Prevention mode inspects and blocks SQL injection at Microsoft's edge, with one policy for every origin. Per-region Application Gateway WAFs work further downstream and multiply the management effort. Azure Firewall IDPS without TLS inspection cannot see inside HTTPS requests, and DDoS Protection handles volumetric and protocol attacks rather than application-layer exploits.

q: Compliance requires encryption in transit between Contoso's datacenter and Azure. The traffic uses an existing provider-based ExpressRoute circuit with private peering. What should you do?
opts: Enable MACsec on the private peering of the existing provider circuit
Run IPsec VPN tunnels over the existing ExpressRoute circuit
Turn on the circuit's encryption setting, which is disabled by default
Enable TLS inspection on Azure Firewall Premium in the hub VNet
why: ExpressRoute is private but not encrypted, so encryption in transit has to be added; IPsec VPN tunnels over the circuit encrypt traffic end to end and work with a provider circuit. MACsec is available on ExpressRoute Direct ports, not on a provider circuit. There is no circuit-level encryption switch, and TLS inspection decrypts and re-encrypts traffic at a firewall rather than encrypting the datacenter-to-Azure path.

q: A hub-and-spoke design places Azure Firewall in the hub VNet. Peering between the hub and each spoke already exists. All outbound internet traffic from every spoke must be inspected by that firewall. What else must you configure?
opts: Allow gateway transit on the hub peering and Use remote gateways on each spoke peering
Allow forwarded traffic on each peering, with no further routing changes
A route table on each spoke subnet with 0.0.0.0/0 and a Virtual appliance next hop set to the firewall's private IP
A service tag-based NSG rule on each spoke subnet that sends internet-bound traffic to the firewall
why: Peering provides connectivity only; a user-defined route sending 0.0.0.0/0 to the firewall's private IP is what forces spoke traffic through the hub. Gateway transit settings are for sharing a VPN or ExpressRoute gateway. Allow forwarded traffic is needed so the firewall's forwarded packets are accepted but does not steer anything, and NSGs allow or deny traffic without ever changing its route.

q: Web and database VMs share one subnet. An NSG rule must allow only the web VMs to reach the database VMs on TCP 1433. VM membership changes often, and the NSG must not need editing when VMs are added or removed. What should you use?
opts: An IP group in Azure Firewall that lists the web VMs' private IP addresses
A source and a destination application security group, with each VM's NIC added to its group
The VirtualNetwork service tag as both the source and the destination of the rule
The subnet's address prefix as the source, with the database VMs' addresses as the destination
why: Application security groups let a rule reference VMs by role, and group membership follows the NICs, so no rule edits are needed as VMs come and go. An IP group still has to be updated by hand and belongs to Azure Firewall, not the NSG. The VirtualNetwork tag matches every address in the network, and the shared subnet prefix cannot distinguish web VMs from database VMs.

q: Salary and national ID columns in an Azure SQL Database must stay encrypted even from administrators who hold sysadmin rights on the server. Keys must be held outside the database, and only a trusted client application may decrypt. What should you implement?
opts: Transparent Data Encryption with a customer-managed key in Key Vault
Column-level encryption with ENCRYPTBYKEY and a database master key
Always Encrypted with the column master key stored in Key Vault
Dynamic Data Masking with UNMASK withheld from the application's users
why: Always Encrypted keeps the column encryption keys outside the database engine, so the engine, and therefore a DBA, only ever sees ciphertext; decryption happens in the client driver. TDE encrypts files at rest but the engine decrypts data for any authorized query. ENCRYPTBYKEY keeps keys inside the database, so a privileged administrator can decrypt. Masking only changes what query results display and does not encrypt stored values.

q: Several Azure-hosted apps share a storage account's access keys. Contoso wants per-app, auditable, least-privilege access to specific containers, with no secret for the apps to store or rotate. What should you do?
opts: Give each app a service SAS tied to a stored access policy, signed with the account key
Assign each app's managed identity the Storage Account Contributor role on the account
Give each app's managed identity a Storage Blob Data role on its container, then disable Shared Key access
Give each app a user delegation SAS that it requests once and stores in its configuration
why: Entra ID authorization with data-plane roles scoped to each container gives per-identity, auditable access with nothing to store, and disabling Shared Key authorization closes the key path. A service SAS is signed with the account key and is still a stored secret. Storage Account Contributor is a management role that can also list the account keys, so it quietly restores full control. A stored user delegation SAS is better than key-based tokens but is still a time-limited secret to keep and renew.

q: A Key Vault uses vault access policies, and several apps read its secrets through those policies. Contoso will switch the vault to the Azure RBAC permission model without interrupting the apps. What should you do first?
opts: Switch the vault now, because existing access policies keep applying alongside role assignments
Enable purge protection, which carries access policies over to the new permission model
Assign each app's identity a data-plane role such as Key Vault Secrets User, then switch the model
Grant each app's identity Contributor on the vault so it can still read secret values after the switch
why: A vault evaluates one permission model at a time, so after the switch access policies are no longer used and apps only work if they already hold equivalent role assignments; assigning those roles first avoids an outage. Access policies do not run alongside RBAC, purge protection is unrelated to authorization, and Contributor is a management-plane role that does not grant access to secret values.

q: MACsec on an ExpressRoute Direct port encrypts the link between a customer's edge routers and Microsoft's edge routers, but does not by itself encrypt traffic end to end between the datacenter and the Azure VM.
opts: True
False
why: MACsec is a layer 2 protection for the physical link into Microsoft's edge. Anything beyond that edge is not covered, so end-to-end encryption still requires IPsec or application-level TLS. The statement sounds like a limitation but it is accurate.

q: For Azure Firewall Premium IDPS signatures to match on the payload of outbound HTTPS requests, TLS inspection must also be enabled on the firewall.
opts: True
False
why: Without decrypting the session the firewall can only see handshake metadata such as destination and server name, not the encrypted payload. TLS inspection is what gives IDPS signatures something to match inside HTTPS.

q: Dynamic Data Masking prevents a user with only SELECT permission from inferring the real values of a masked column by running repeated filtered queries.
opts: True
False
why: Masking is applied to query results only, so filters and comparisons still run against the real stored data. A user without UNMASK permission can narrow down values with WHERE clauses, which is why masking is a display-layer convenience and not a substitute for encryption or permissions.

q: In a Key Vault that uses the Azure RBAC permission model, holding the Contributor role on the vault does not by itself allow a user to read secret values.
opts: True
False
why: Contributor is a management-plane role over the vault resource. Reading secrets requires a data-plane role such as Key Vault Secrets User, so a Contributor who is not granted one cannot read values (under the older access policy model, by contrast, a Contributor could edit access policies and grant themselves access).

q: Contoso plans to use Azure Bastion to reach VMs that have only private IP addresses. Which two statements describe the design? (Choose two.)
opts: The target VMs must be placed in the AzureBastionSubnet
Bastion decrypts and inspects the session traffic with IDPS signatures
Bastion is deployed into a dedicated subnet named AzureBastionSubnet
NSGs on the VM subnets are unnecessary once Bastion is deployed
NSGs on the VM subnets must allow RDP or SSH from the Bastion subnet's address range
why: Bastion needs its own subnet named AzureBastionSubnet, and because it connects to targets over their private IPs, the target subnets' NSGs must still permit RDP or SSH from the Bastion subnet. The VMs live in their own subnets, Bastion proxies sessions rather than inspecting them, and NSGs remain the control that scopes who can reach the VMs.

q: Contoso adds an Azure DDoS Protection plan for public-facing workloads in a virtual network. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: It blocks SQL injection and cross-site scripting at layer 7
The plan is associated with virtual networks and covers the public IP addresses of resources in them
It must be enabled individually on each VM in the virtual network
It provides attack telemetry and mitigation reports through Azure Monitor
It protects the public endpoints of PaaS services such as storage accounts
why: The DDoS Protection plan is linked to virtual networks and protects the public IPs of resources inside them, with metrics and mitigation reports available in Azure Monitor. It mitigates volumetric and protocol attacks, so application-layer exploits such as SQL injection need a WAF. It is not enabled per VM, and PaaS public endpoints outside your VNet are not covered by it.

q: Contoso implements Always Encrypted for sensitive Azure SQL columns, with the column master key in Azure Key Vault. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Applications must use a supported client driver with column encryption enabled in the connection
The database engine decrypts the values in memory to evaluate any T-SQL function on the column
Transparent Data Encryption must be disabled before Always Encrypted can be used
The column master key is stored outside the database, so database administrators cannot decrypt the data
Data is encrypted only at rest and is decrypted on the server before it is sent to the client
why: Always Encrypted relies on a client driver that encrypts and decrypts transparently, and the master key lives in Key Vault, so the database engine and its administrators never hold the means to decrypt. The engine cannot compute arbitrary functions on ciphertext, TDE can run alongside it, and data stays encrypted in transit and in memory on the server rather than being decrypted there.

q: A private endpoint is created for an Azure SQL Database, but application servers in the peered VNet still resolve the database's fully qualified domain name to its public IP address instead of the private endpoint's private IP. What is most likely missing?
opts: The application servers need a public IP address assigned first, since private endpoints route return traffic through the VM's own public interface
Private endpoints do not support Azure SQL Database as a resource type; only storage accounts and Key Vault support this feature
The private endpoint needs a corresponding Azure Private DNS zone (or custom DNS override) linked to the VNet so the FQDN resolves to the private IP
A service endpoint must be enabled first on the subnet before a private endpoint for the same resource can take effect
why: A private endpoint only creates the private IP; name resolution for the database's FQDN still has to be pointed at that private IP, typically through an Azure Private DNS zone (or a custom on-premises DNS override) linked to the VNet. Without that DNS piece in place, clients keep resolving the public IP even though the private endpoint exists. Azure SQL Database is a supported private endpoint resource type, application servers do not need a public IP to reach a private endpoint, and a service endpoint is a separate, unrelated mechanism, not a prerequisite for a private endpoint.

q: A company must keep financial records in Blob Storage for 7 years so that no one, including the account owner, can modify or delete them until the period expires. Which configuration meets this?
opts: An unlocked time-based retention policy of 7 years applied to the container
A legal hold with a tag applied to the container and cleared after 7 years
Soft delete with 365-day retention plus blob versioning on the storage account
A locked time-based retention policy of 7 years applied to the container
why: A locked time-based retention policy gives WORM protection: blobs cannot be modified or deleted and the retention interval cannot be shortened, even by the account owner. An unlocked policy is intended for testing and can still be changed or removed by a privileged user. A legal hold has no expiry and can be cleared by someone with permission, and soft delete with versioning only makes deleted data recoverable for a limited period.

q: NSG flow logs capture the packet payloads of denied connections, so an analyst can inspect the content of blocked attack traffic.
opts: True
False
why: Flow logs record connection metadata such as source and destination address, ports, protocol, direction and the allow or deny decision, never packet contents. Inspecting payloads needs a packet capture or an inspecting firewall.

q: A VM cannot reach another VM on TCP 443. You must identify which NSG rule is blocking this specific flow, right now, without enabling logging and waiting. What should you use?
opts: Enable NSG flow logs and review the aggregated results in Traffic Analytics
Run IP flow verify in Network Watcher with the VM, direction, protocol, and addresses
Start a packet capture on the destination VM and filter on port 443
Open the effective routes table for the source VM's network interface
why: IP flow verify evaluates a single 5-tuple against the NSG rules applied to the VM and returns whether it is allowed or denied and the name of the rule responsible. Flow logs with Traffic Analytics show historical traffic once logging is enabled, a capture on the destination sees nothing if the packets are dropped before arrival, and effective routes describe next hops rather than security rules.

q: A WAF policy on Application Gateway has run in Detection mode for a week. Logs show a SQL injection rule matching a legitimate JSON field in the checkout request. What should you do before switching to Prevention mode?
opts: Disable the entire SQL injection rule group, then switch to Prevention mode
Add an exclusion for that request attribute on the matching rule, then switch to Prevention mode
Leave the policy in Detection mode and add NSG rules that block the client IP addresses it flags
Add a custom rule that allows all requests from the IP ranges customers commonly use
why: A WAF exclusion tunes out the false positive for that one attribute and rule while leaving the rest of the protection intact, which is the normal Detection-to-Prevention tuning step. Disabling the whole rule group removes protection for every request, and an allow rule for customer IP ranges bypasses inspection for all traffic from them. Detection mode never blocks, and NSG rules acting on flagged IPs are reactive and unrelated to the false positive.

q: Contoso users upload files to a blob container. Security wants uploaded files scanned for malware, with alerts surfaced in Defender for Cloud, without changing the uploading application. What should you do?
opts: Enable blob versioning and the change feed so infected uploads can be rolled back
Enable Microsoft Defender for Servers on the VMs that upload the files
Restrict the storage account firewall to allow uploads only from the corporate subnet
Enable Microsoft Defender for Storage with malware scanning on the storage account
why: Defender for Storage with malware scanning inspects blobs as they are uploaded and raises alerts in Defender for Cloud, with no application change. Versioning and the change feed help recover from changes but do not detect malware. Defender for Servers protects the VMs themselves, not the files stored in the account, and a firewall rule limits where uploads come from without inspecting what they contain.

q: Compliance requires a durable record of the statements executed against an Azure SQL logical server's databases, retained in a Log Analytics workspace for one year. What should you configure?
opts: Server-level Azure SQL auditing sending events to a workspace with one-year retention
Defender for SQL advanced threat protection, with alerts exported to the workspace
Query Store on each database, which keeps runtime statistics for performance analysis
A weekly SQL vulnerability assessment scan with results stored in the workspace
why: Azure SQL auditing records database and server events and can write them to a Log Analytics workspace, where retention is set to meet the one-year requirement. Defender for SQL alerts on suspicious activity rather than keeping a complete record, Query Store holds performance statistics rather than an audit trail, and a vulnerability assessment reports misconfigurations at the time of a scan.

q: A company wants to publish its own custom application, running behind a Standard Load Balancer, so that other business units in different virtual networks can connect to it privately without it ever being exposed to the public internet. A private endpoint created by each consuming VNet is sufficient on its own, with nothing additional required on the publishing side.
opts: True
False
why: The publishing side needs a Private Link service configured on top of the Standard Load Balancer; consumers then create private endpoints to reach it. A private endpoint alone is only the consuming half of that connection — without a Private Link service to publish the application, there is nothing for those private endpoints to privately connect to.

q: Contoso enables Azure SQL auditing for a logical server. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A server-level audit policy applies to all databases on the server
Audit events are blocked from running until an analyst reviews them
Audit events can be written to a storage account, a Log Analytics workspace or an event hub
Defender for SQL must be enabled before auditing can be configured
Audit records cannot be retained for longer than 90 days
why: A server-level audit policy covers every database on the server, and auditing supports storage, Log Analytics and Event Hubs as destinations. Auditing records events and does not block or hold statements, it is independent of Defender for SQL (a separate plan), and retention depends on the destination configured, not a fixed 90-day cap.

q: An administrator with Key Vault permissions deletes a production key before leaving the company. Soft-delete is enabled but purge protection is not. Security wants to ensure that, in future, no identity can permanently remove a deleted key before retention ends. What should you do?
opts: Increase the soft-delete retention period to 90 days
Apply a CanNotDelete resource lock to the vault
Enable purge protection on the vault
Back up each key and keep the backup in a second vault in another region
why: Purge protection blocks permanent deletion of soft-deleted objects until the retention period ends, even for identities with purge permission. A longer retention window only lengthens the time an authorized identity can still purge the key. A resource lock protects the vault resource, not objects inside it, and a backup in another vault is a recovery copy that does not prevent the purge.

q: A user delegation SAS is signed with a key obtained through Microsoft Entra ID credentials, so rotating the storage account access keys does not invalidate it.
opts: True
False
why: Service and account SAS tokens are signed with the account key and stop working when it is rotated. A user delegation SAS is signed with a user delegation key issued to an Entra identity, and its effective permissions are limited by that identity's role assignments.

q: Contoso reviews Key Vault protection settings for production vaults. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: After purge protection is enabled it cannot be turned off for that vault
The vault owner can disable purge protection in an emergency to purge a key early
A soft-deleted key can no longer be recovered once purge protection is enabled
A soft-deleted key can still be recovered during retention when purge protection is on
Purge protection can be enabled only on vaults that have soft-delete disabled
why: Purge protection is irreversible once enabled and only blocks permanent deletion; recovery of soft-deleted objects during the retention period still works normally. It builds on soft-delete rather than excluding it, and because nobody can turn it off, not even the owner can purge a key early.

q: A partner receives a service SAS for a blob container. If the token leaks, Contoso wants to cancel it immediately without rotating the storage account keys that other apps use. How should the SAS have been created?
opts: As an ad hoc SAS with a one-year expiry
As an account SAS with all permissions
By referencing a stored access policy on the container
By sharing the primary account key instead
why: A SAS tied to a stored access policy can be revoked by deleting or editing the policy, with no key rotation. An ad hoc SAS can only be invalidated by rotating the key that signed it, which affects other apps. An account SAS is signed with the key and has the same limitation, and sharing the account key is the least safe option.

q: Contoso wants to remove SQL password logins from an Azure SQL logical server and require only Microsoft Entra identities. Which setting does this?
opts: Transparent data encryption with a customer-managed key
Microsoft Entra-only authentication
Dynamic data masking on the sensitive columns
The server firewall allow-list
why: Entra-only authentication disables SQL authentication on the server so only Entra identities can sign in. TDE protects data at rest, masking hides values from query results and the firewall decides which networks can connect; none of them removes SQL logins.

q: Contoso must keep Azure SQL Managed Instance audit records for seven years and also query recent events for detections. Which two destinations meet this? (Choose two.)
opts: A Log Analytics workspace for queries and Sentinel analytics
A storage account for long retention
The SQL error log on the instance
A Key Vault secret holding the audit text
why: SQL auditing can write to storage for cheap long retention and to Log Analytics for queries and detections (and to Event Hubs for streaming). The SQL error log is not an audit store, and Key Vault is for secrets, not log data.

q: Contoso runs PostgreSQL flexible servers in Azure and on Amazon RDS and wants to detect brute-force attempts and anomalous queries on both. Which Defender for Cloud plan applies?
opts: Defender for Storage
Defender for open-source relational databases
Defender for SQL servers on machines
Defender for Azure Cosmos DB
why: The open-source relational databases plan covers Azure Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL flexible servers and Amazon RDS databases. SQL servers on machines targets SQL Server on VMs, Cosmos DB has its own plan and Defender for Storage protects storage accounts.

q: A central security team must block inbound RDP and SSH on every virtual network in 40 subscriptions, while application teams keep managing their own NSGs. Which service fits?
opts: Service endpoint policies attached to each subnet that reaches storage
Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules
Azure Firewall DNAT rules deployed in each regional hub virtual network
An NSG on every subnet, with each application team maintaining its own rules
why: Security admin rules apply organization-wide to the virtual networks in a network group and are evaluated before NSG rules, so the central team can enforce the block while teams keep their NSGs. Per-subnet NSGs are exactly the decentralized model, DNAT rules publish services rather than block ports, and service endpoint policies control storage access.

q: Azure Virtual Network Manager allows several security admin configurations to be deployed to the same region, each with its own rules.
opts: True
False
why: Only one security admin configuration can be deployed per region. To organize more rules, add multiple rule collections inside that single configuration.

q: Branch offices and spoke VNets connect through an Azure Virtual WAN hub, and all traffic between them and to the internet must be inspected by a firewall managed centrally. What should be deployed?
opts: Azure Firewall in the hub, making it a secured hub managed with Azure Firewall Manager
A DDoS protection plan applied to the public IPs, with no firewall at all
A network security group attached to every subnet inside the hub
An Azure Bastion host deployed in each spoke virtual network
why: Converting the Virtual WAN hub into a secured hub places Azure Firewall in it, and Firewall Manager policies control the rules centrally. NSGs cannot be applied to hub-managed subnets in this way, Bastion provides remote administration rather than traffic inspection, and DDoS protection does not inspect flows.

q: Remote staff must connect to an Azure VNet by VPN and be subject to Conditional Access and MFA. Which point-to-site configuration supports this?
opts: Microsoft Entra ID authentication with the OpenVPN tunnel type
A site-to-site IPsec tunnel to each remote worker with a pre-shared key
Certificate authentication with the SSTP tunnel type and a root certificate on every client
RADIUS authentication against an on-premises server with the IKEv2 tunnel type
why: Entra ID authentication is supported with OpenVPN, and it brings Conditional Access and MFA to VPN sign-in. Certificates and RADIUS are other authentication types that do not use Entra Conditional Access directly, and a site-to-site tunnel connects networks rather than individual users.

q: Contoso wants to retire its VPN for access to internal web apps and file shares by using Microsoft Entra, with stricter Conditional Access for only the finance servers. How should this be configured?
opts: A new Azure Firewall application rule collection for the finance server addresses
Azure Bastion deployed in front of each server for the administrators
Only Quick Access with every internal server and file share listed in it
Entra Private Access with a per-app Global Secure Access app for the finance servers
why: Private Access uses the Global Secure Access client and a private network connector, and a per-app Global Secure Access app lets the finance servers have their own users and Conditional Access policies, separate from the general Quick Access group. Quick Access alone applies one policy set to everything, Bastion is for admin access to VMs, and a firewall rule collection does not provide per-user private app access.

q: Traffic from a VM to a SQL private endpoint is blocked although the VM's NSG allows it. The admin wants a tool that tests a specific flow and names the deciding rule. Which should be used?
opts: Azure Monitor metrics for the VM
Defender for Cloud secure score
Network Watcher topology view
Network Watcher NSG diagnostics
why: NSG diagnostics simulates a flow between a source and destination and reports allowed or denied with the exact rule responsible, including NSGs at different association levels. Topology shows relationships, metrics show performance, and secure score summarizes posture.

q: A pipeline redeploys several App Service apps and Functions daily. All of them need the same Key Vault role, the role assignment must not have to be recreated after a redeployment, and no credential may be stored. What should you create?
opts: A system-assigned identity on each resource, with the role reassigned by the pipeline after every deployment
A system-assigned identity on each resource, added to a security group that holds the role assignment
A service principal with a certificate, shared among the resources through a Key Vault reference
A user-assigned managed identity with the role assigned once, attached to each resource
why: A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone resource, so one role assignment survives redeployments and is shared by every resource it is attached to. A system-assigned identity is created and deleted with its resource, so a redeployment produces a new principal that needs the role again, either by the pipeline or through group re-membership. A shared service principal certificate is still a credential that has to be stored and protected.

q: Contoso must prevent privileged containers from being scheduled on every AKS cluster in a subscription and report non-compliance centrally in Azure. What should you use?
opts: Defender for Containers runtime threat detection, with alerts for privileged containers
Kubernetes network policies that deny traffic to and from privileged pods
Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization, removing the permission to create privileged pods
Azure Policy for Kubernetes with the built-in privileged container policy set to Deny
why: Azure Policy for Kubernetes enforces admission control with a Deny effect, so non-compliant pods are never scheduled, and it reports compliance across clusters in the Azure Policy view. Defender for Containers detects and alerts after the fact. Network policies control traffic between pods, not what pod configuration is allowed, and Kubernetes RBAC governs which users can call the API rather than which pod specifications are acceptable.

q: A VM's managed disks use server-side encryption with platform-managed keys. A new requirement says the temporary disk and host caches must also be encrypted, with nothing to configure inside the guest OS. What should you do?
opts: Assign a disk encryption set with a customer-managed key to the disks
Switch the managed disks to double encryption at rest
Deploy Azure Disk Encryption with a key encryption key
Turn on encryption at host for the VM
why: Encryption at host encrypts the temporary disk and caches at the host before data reaches storage, with no guest configuration. Customer-managed keys and double encryption change who holds the keys or add a layer to the managed disks only, and neither covers the temporary disk or host caches. Azure Disk Encryption works through BitLocker or DM-Crypt inside the guest, which the requirement excludes.

q: An App Service app serves a B2B API over HTTPS. Requests that do not present a client certificate must be rejected before they reach the application code. What should you configure?
opts: Set the incoming client certificate mode to Optional
Enable HTTPS Only and set the minimum inbound TLS version to 1.2
Bind a custom domain to the app with an SNI SSL certificate
Set the incoming client certificate mode to Require
why: Client certificate mode set to Require makes the platform reject connections that present no certificate, which is the mutual TLS requirement. Optional lets requests without a certificate through to the app, HTTPS Only and a minimum TLS version protect the server side of the connection without asking who the client is, and a domain binding certificate identifies the server to its callers.

q: A Foundry agent only needs to read from one Azure AI Search index and call a single downstream pricing API. Which approach follows least privilege?
opts: Reuse the Foundry project's managed identity, which already has access to every resource connected to the project
Give the agent its own identity with a read-only data role on the search service and permission to call only the pricing API
Give the agent's identity Search Service Contributor so it can adjust the index if the schema changes
Run the agent with a developer's identity so access changes follow that person's role
why: Its own identity, limited to read-only data access and one API, keeps the agent's reach equal to its task, so a prompt injection cannot be used to touch anything else. The project's shared identity inherits access to every connected resource, Search Service Contributor is a management role the agent does not need, and a developer's identity brings that person's broad access along and blurs attribution.

q: A security team wants an agent registered under Microsoft Entra Agent ID to be able to authenticate only from the organization's trusted network locations. Which control should be applied?
opts: A Conditional Access policy for all users that excludes service accounts
A PIM eligible assignment, with MFA on activation, for the role the agent uses
A Conditional Access policy targeting agent identities with a named location condition
An Azure Policy deny assignment on the resource group that hosts the agent's compute
why: Conditional Access can be scoped to agent identities and evaluate conditions such as network location before an agent is allowed to authenticate. A policy for users does not apply to agent identities, and excluding service accounts removes the very identities in question. PIM governs time-bound role activation, and Azure Policy governs resource configuration, not sign-in conditions.

q: Defender XDR flags an agent identity as potentially compromised. Before containment, the team needs the full set of data sources, APIs and downstream agents that identity could reach, not only what it has called so far. What provides this?
opts: Attack path analysis in Defender for Cloud
Blast radius analysis for the agent identity
Entra sign-in logs filtered to the agent's service principal
An access review of the agent's group memberships
why: Blast radius analysis maps what a specific identity can reach, which scopes containment to the real exposure. Attack path analysis models exploitable chains across cloud resources rather than one identity's reachable scope. Sign-in logs show only authentications that already happened, and an access review of group membership covers one input to access, not APIs and agents the identity can invoke.

q: Contoso wants per-team token quotas and centralized logging for several Foundry model deployments, without changing any agent code. What should you implement?
opts: Content filters with a lower severity threshold on each deployment
Different managed identities per team, each with a custom RBAC role that limits tokens
API Management as an AI gateway in front of the deployments, using token-limit policies and logging
A Conditional Access session control that limits request volume per team
why: An AI gateway built on API Management sits in front of the deployments and applies cross-cutting policies such as authentication, token limits and logging in one place, without touching agents. Content filters judge harmful content, not quota. RBAC roles grant or deny access and cannot meter tokens, and Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions, not API request volume.

q: A Foundry agent summarizes documents that partners upload, and occasionally follows instructions hidden inside them. Which control detects this attack before the content reaches the model?
opts: Raise the severity thresholds on the hate and violence content filters
Narrow the agent identity's permissions to the one document store it needs
Configure Prompt Shields to scan the retrieved documents
Place the search service behind a private endpoint with public access off
why: Prompt Shields inspects grounding documents for indirect prompt injection before they influence the model. Content filter categories look for harmful content, and hidden instructions are often not harmful in themselves. Narrower permissions limit what a successful attack can do rather than detecting it, and a private endpoint controls network reachability of the search service.

q: A SharePoint site shared with 'Everyone' years ago holds sensitive content. After Microsoft 365 Copilot is enabled, employees see that content in answers. What addresses the root cause with the least disruption to other users?
opts: Turn off Copilot for every user until the next quarterly access review
Create a DLP policy that stops Copilot from using any SharePoint content
Require a compliant device in Conditional Access for Copilot sign-ins
Remove the Everyone sharing from the site and label its sensitive content
why: Copilot only surfaces what a user is already permitted to see, so the cause is the overbroad permission; removing the broad sharing and labeling sensitive content fixes it for Copilot and every other search path. Disabling Copilot or blocking all SharePoint content is far more disruptive and leaves the oversharing in place. A device requirement does not change who is permitted to see the content.

q: Contoso wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to stop using files labeled Highly Confidential in its responses, even for users who have permission to open those files. Which control fits?
opts: A retention label that deletes Highly Confidential files after 30 days
A Purview DLP policy for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location that matches the sensitivity label
An Insider Risk Management policy that flags users who open Highly Confidential files
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA and a compliant device for Copilot
why: A DLP policy that targets the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can exclude labeled content from Copilot's responses even when the user's permissions would allow access. A retention label deletes content on a schedule rather than controlling Copilot's use of it, Insider Risk Management detects risky behavior without blocking anything, and Conditional Access controls the sign-in, not what content Copilot draws on.

q: A maker builds a custom agent in Copilot Studio. Admins want prompts and responses evaluated against security policies while the agent is running, not only when it is published. What should they enable?
opts: Real-time protection for the Copilot Studio agent
A Power Platform data policy that restricts which connectors the agent can use
An approval step that reviews the agent before it is published
A sensitivity label on the agent's knowledge sources
why: Real-time protection evaluates prompts and responses as the agent runs, which is the runtime check described. A data policy limits which connectors can be combined, a publish approval is a one-time gate before release, and a sensitivity label on knowledge sources classifies content without inspecting live prompts and responses.

q: An agent grounds its answers in a vector index built from confidential documents. A security review concludes that access is well controlled because only a defined group can chat with the agent. What gap does the review most likely miss?
opts: Whether the chat front end signs users in with a phishing-resistant authentication strength
Whether the search index and its source storage restrict direct access to identities that should read them
Whether the model deployment has a content filter configured with a strict threshold
Whether the agent's conversation logs are retained for at least 90 days
