why: Controlling who can chat says nothing about who can query the index or open the underlying files directly; the grounding store is a sensitive asset with its own access controls. Sign-in strength for the chat app, content filtering of responses and log retention are all valid hardening topics, but none of them closes direct access to the data.

q: A support agent runs under a service principal shared with 12 other automations, and that principal holds broad API permissions. Defender flags the agent as compromised. What is the main problem with this design?
opts: Service principals cannot be disabled, so a compromised agent cannot be contained at all
Conditional Access cannot be applied to any service principal, so no sign-in restrictions are possible
Containing the agent also affects the 12 automations that share the identity, and its actions cannot be attributed separately
Service principals cannot authenticate with certificates, so the agent must rely on a stored client secret
why: A shared identity blends the agent's actions with everything else that uses it, so containment either breaks the other automations or leaves the agent running, and investigators cannot attribute activity to it. A dedicated agent identity can be scoped, governed and disabled on its own. The other statements are false: service principals can be disabled, can be targeted by Conditional Access for workload identities, and can use certificates.

q: Using a disk encryption set with a customer-managed key for a VM's managed disks requires Azure Disk Encryption to be enabled on the VM.
opts: True
False
why: A disk encryption set with a customer-managed key is server-side encryption with your own key and is configured on the managed disks. Azure Disk Encryption is a separate guest-level mechanism using BitLocker or DM-Crypt, and neither depends on the other.

q: Because an AI agent is not a human user, Conditional Access policies cannot be applied to its Microsoft Entra Agent ID identity.
opts: True
False
why: Agent identities are governed like any other identity, and Conditional Access can evaluate conditions such as network location before an agent is allowed to authenticate. Being non-human is a reason to apply controls, not an exemption from them.

q: Deploying an AI Gateway with Azure API Management in front of Microsoft Foundry agents removes the need to apply Conditional Access to those agents' identities.
opts: True
False
why: An AI Gateway centralizes traffic-level controls like authentication enforcement, rate limiting, and logging — it does not replace identity-level Conditional Access policies applied to the agent identities themselves; the two are complementary layers, not substitutes.

q: If the Everyone sharing on a SharePoint site is removed, content from that site stops appearing in Microsoft 365 Copilot answers for users who no longer have permission to it.
opts: True
False
why: Copilot returns only content the signed-in user is already authorized to access, so correcting the underlying permission corrects what Copilot can surface. It sounds like it should need a Copilot-specific setting, but Copilot does not hold a separate permission model.

q: Giving an AI agent its own dedicated identity limits the damage of a compromise only if that identity's permissions are also scoped: a dedicated identity holding Contributor on a subscription can reach as much as a shared identity with the same role.
opts: True
False
why: A dedicated identity improves attribution and lets you contain one agent, but reach is determined by permissions. Least-privilege scoping is what shrinks the blast radius.

q: Contoso wants to stop privileged pods from being deployed to an AKS cluster and to limit which pods in the cluster can talk to the database pods. Which two controls should it use? (Choose two.)
opts: Defender for Containers alerts, which block privileged pods at admission
An NSG on the node subnet, which filters traffic between pods on the same node
Kubernetes network policies that allow only the application pods to reach the database pods
Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization, which restricts pod-to-pod connections
Azure Policy for Kubernetes with the privileged container policy set to Deny
why: Azure Policy for Kubernetes enforces what pod configurations are admitted, and network policies restrict which pods may communicate. Defender for Containers detects and alerts but does not block at admission, an NSG on the node subnet does not see traffic between pods on one node, and Kubernetes authorization controls API operations rather than pod networking.

q: Contoso runs 200 support agents created from one template and needs consistent controls with per-agent attribution. Which two statements about Microsoft Entra Agent ID are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Agent identities are exempt from Conditional Access because they are not human users
Each agent has its own identity, so its actions can be audited and it can be contained alone
All agents created from one blueprint share a single token and one sign-in session
Permissions and Conditional Access set on the blueprint apply to every agent created from it
Blueprints remove the need to scope each agent's permissions to least privilege
why: Agent Identity gives each agent an individual identity for attribution and containment, and blueprints let policy and permissions be applied once and inherited across a fleet. Agents are not exempt from Conditional Access, they do not share a session, and a blueprint is a way to apply least privilege at scale, not a substitute for it.

q: Before rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot, Contoso wants to reduce the chance that sensitive content appears in answers. Which two actions help? (Choose two.)
opts: Place an NSG in front of the Copilot service so that it cannot read sensitive files
Remove overly broad sharing from SharePoint sites that hold sensitive content
Require a compliant device for every Copilot sign-in across the organization
Assign Copilot licenses only to administrators until the rollout is complete
Apply a Purview DLP policy for the Copilot location that matches sensitivity labels
why: Copilot honors existing permissions, so removing oversharing reduces what it can find, and a DLP policy for the Copilot location can exclude labeled content even where permission exists. An NSG filters network traffic and cannot see Copilot content, a device requirement does not change what a permitted user may see, and limiting licenses to administrators removes the feature rather than securing it.

q: A financial services company wants to run a sensitive AI inferencing workload so that even Microsoft, as the cloud operator, cannot access the data or model weights while they are being processed in memory. Which Azure capability should they use?
opts: Server-side encryption with platform-managed keys on the underlying managed disk, protecting data at rest without any guest OS configuration
Encryption at host for the VM, extending platform encryption to temporary disks and in-memory caches at the host level
Azure Disk Encryption using BitLocker inside the guest OS, protecting the OS and data disks at the file-system level
Azure confidential computing, using confidential VMs or containers with hardware-based trusted execution environments
why: Confidential computing is specifically designed to protect data in use, isolating memory contents inside a hardware-based trusted execution environment so that not even the cloud operator can access it during processing. Server-side encryption, encryption at host, and Azure Disk Encryption all protect data at rest, on disk, or in the host's storage layer -- none of them protect data while it is actively being processed in memory the way confidential computing does.

q: Contoso wants its AKS clusters to run only container images that come from its approved Azure Container Registry. The restriction must be enforced when a pod is scheduled. What should you use?
opts: Azure Policy for Kubernetes with the allowed container images policy set to Deny
Defender for Containers vulnerability assessment on the registry
A private endpoint for the registry, with public access disabled
A Kubernetes network policy that limits egress to the registry's IP range
why: The Azure Policy add-on enforces admission control, so a pod that references an image outside the allowed registry pattern is rejected at scheduling time. Vulnerability assessment reports on images and does not block them, a private endpoint only controls how the registry is reached and does not stop a cluster from pulling from other registries, and an egress rule limits network paths without evaluating the pod specification.

q: Prompt Shields can detect indirect prompt injection hidden in a retrieved document, even when that text would not be flagged by harm-category content filters.
opts: True
False
why: Content filters score content for categories such as hate or violence, while injected instructions can look entirely benign as text. Prompt Shields specifically evaluates whether prompts or grounding content are attempting to manipulate the model.

q: A Foundry agent calls an external partner API that supports only a static API key. Three other agents use the same key from a shared Key Vault secret. After the agent is flagged as compromised, investigators cannot tell which agent made which partner calls. What should Contoso change?
opts: Route the calls through an API Management gateway that authenticates each agent's own identity and logs by caller
Rotate the shared key every week while all four agents continue to read the same Key Vault secret
Copy the key into the Foundry project's application settings so that it is easier to rotate
Add the four agent identities to a security group that holds the Key Vault Secrets User role
why: Per-agent attribution requires each agent to be identifiable when it makes the call, which a gateway authenticating each agent's own identity provides while the partner key stays behind it. Rotating a shared key or moving it into settings leaves every agent indistinguishable, and a group with a Key Vault role changes who can read the secret without changing the fact that all four agents present the same key.

q: Memory contents of an Azure confidential VM are protected from the cloud operator, but an administrator inside the guest operating system can still read them.
opts: True
False
why: Confidential computing isolates data in use from the host and the cloud operator using hardware-based trusted execution. An administrator within the guest OS has legitimate access to the VM's own memory, so guest access control remains your responsibility.

q: A DevSecOps team wants images pushed to Azure Container Registry scanned for known vulnerabilities, plus ongoing runtime threat detection for the containers running in AKS. Which single Defender for Cloud plan covers both?
opts: Defender for Servers
Defender CSPM
Defender for Containers
Defender for App Service
why: Defender for Containers combines image vulnerability assessment for registries with runtime threat detection for Kubernetes workloads. Defender CSPM provides posture management and attack path analysis but not runtime threat detection, Defender for Servers protects VMs, and Defender for App Service covers web apps rather than registries and clusters.

q: A Foundry agent's identity is already scoped to one document index and one API. The team now wants to restrict which categories of harmful output the agent may produce while it runs, independent of what it can reach. Which control addresses this?
opts: Narrow the agent identity's permissions further in Microsoft Entra Agent ID
Require a phishing-resistant authentication strength when the agent's identity signs in
Use a private endpoint so the model deployment is reachable only from the VNet
Configure content filters in Foundry guardrails for harmful output categories
why: Guardrails and content filters control what the agent may say or do at runtime, separately from what its identity can reach. Narrower permissions still address reach, authentication strength governs how the identity signs in, and a private endpoint controls network access to the model, so none of them constrain generated output.

q: AI security posture management (AI-SPM) in Defender for Cloud focuses on detecting an active jailbreak attempt against a deployed agent in real time, the same role Defender for AI Services plays.
opts: True
False
why: AI-SPM is a posture capability, discovering AI workloads, models, and their data stores and surfacing risks like an overly permissive identity before any attack occurs. Defender for AI Services is the one that detects an active runtime threat like a live jailbreak attempt; the two are complementary but play different roles.

q: Contoso evaluates Defender for Cloud capabilities for its Foundry deployments. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: AI security posture management inventories AI workloads and recommends hardening steps
AI security posture management blocks jailbreak prompts inline before they reach the model
Threat protection for AI services alerts on suspected jailbreak attempts against deployed models
Threat protection for AI services applies content filter thresholds to model outputs
Both capabilities require the agent code to call a Defender SDK
why: AI security posture management is the discovery and hardening layer that surfaces risks before an attack, while threat protection for AI services is the runtime layer that alerts on suspected attacks such as jailbreaks. Posture management does not inspect prompts inline, content filtering is a Foundry and Content Safety feature rather than a Defender one, and neither requires agent code changes.

q: An AI agent generates a response that, while triggering no jailbreak or injected-instruction pattern, still describes graphic violence in detail because the grounding document itself contained that content. Which Azure AI Content Safety capability is designed to catch this specific case?
opts: Prompt Shields, since any harmful output must have originated from an injected instruction hidden in the grounding content
Microsoft Entra Agent ID, since the agent's own identity and permission scope determine what kind of content it is allowed to generate
Content filtering, which scores the output against severity categories like violence and blocks it once a configured threshold is exceeded
Blast radius analysis, since it maps everything the agent could reach or had recently accessed if its identity were compromised
why: Content filtering evaluates output against harmful-content severity categories like violence, independent of whether any instruction was trying to manipulate the model — exactly this case. Prompt Shields specifically targets jailbreak and injection attempts, which this scenario explicitly rules out, and Entra Agent ID and blast radius analysis govern identity and post-compromise reach, not the content of a generated response.

q: An Azure OpenAI resource is reachable from any public IP and is authenticated by a key leaked in a repository. Security requires that it not be reachable from the public internet at all, with callers running in Azure VNets. What should you do?
opts: Rotate the key and store the new one in Key Vault
Allow only the corporate public IP range in the resource's networking firewall
Disable key-based authentication and require Microsoft Entra ID authentication
Create a private endpoint and disable public network access for the resource
why: A private endpoint with public network access disabled removes the resource from the public internet entirely. Rotating the key addresses one leaked credential, an IP allow list still leaves a public endpoint reachable from the allowed addresses, and requiring Entra ID authentication is a strong identity control but does not change network reachability.

q: Azure AI Content Safety's severity-based content filtering and Prompt Shields both evaluate the same thing: whether an incoming prompt is attempting to jailbreak the underlying model.
opts: True
False
why: Content filtering judges whether input or output content is harmful by category and severity, while Prompt Shields specifically judges whether a prompt or piece of grounding content is attempting a jailbreak or injection — different questions, not the same evaluation duplicated under two names.

q: Contoso wants to find overexposed SharePoint content before AI agents are broadly deployed. Which two capabilities help? (Choose two.)
opts: Azure Bastion session recording
SharePoint Advanced Management data access governance reports
A Microsoft Purview DSPM data risk assessment of SharePoint sites
A Network Watcher IP flow verify test
why: DSPM data risk assessments and SharePoint Advanced Management data access governance reports identify overshared sites and sharing patterns. Bastion recording and IP flow verify concern VM access and network traffic, not content exposure.

q: Defender for Cloud alerts on Foundry agents show masked content in the evidence section, so analysts cannot see the suspicious prompt. What should be enabled?
opts: AI model security scanning of the models in the Azure Machine Learning registry
The user prompt evidence component of the AI services plan
Data security for AI interactions, which lets Purview analyze prompts and responses
Defender for Key Vault
why: When prompt evidence is off, detection continues but the prompt and response snippets are masked in alerts; enabling it shows the suspicious portions with sensitive data redacted. Purview integration provides data security analysis, model scanning checks registered models, and Key Vault protection is unrelated.

q: Contoso enables threat protection for AI services on a subscription. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: Enabling it requires the Owner or Contributor role on the subscription
AI model security scans models registered in Azure Machine Learning registries for issues such as malware and unsafe serialization
The Purview data security component is included in the plan at no extra license cost
It replaces the need for Foundry guardrails
why: The plan is turned on at subscription scope by an Owner or Contributor, and AI model security scans models in Azure ML registries. The Purview data security integration needs a separate Purview license, and runtime threat detection complements, but does not replace, guardrails that shape what an agent can say or do.

q: A security lead wants one view showing which storage accounts, databases and AI services across subscriptions lack Defender protection, with their critical alerts and internet exposure. Which feature?
opts: A custom workbook from the Azure Monitor workbook gallery, built query by query
The Data and AI security dashboard in Defender for Cloud
The Network Watcher topology view for each virtual network
Microsoft Secure Score in the Microsoft 365 Defender portal for the Microsoft 365 tenant
why: The Data and AI security dashboard summarizes coverage, top issues, sensitive data findings and internet-exposed data and AI resources per subscription. Workbooks, topology and Microsoft 365 Secure Score are not designed for protection coverage of data and AI resources.

q: An agent in Foundry reads partner-uploaded documents, and a document contains hidden text telling it to call a tool that exports customer records. Which guardrail intervention point can stop the exploit before the tool runs?
opts: Tool call
Network egress logging
Output
User input
why: The tool call intervention point scans the action and data an agent proposes to send to a tool, so it can block the export. Output scanning happens after the agent already acted, user input covers the direct prompt rather than the document's content, and logging does not prevent anything.

q: A Foundry guardrail's tool call and tool response intervention points apply to both models and agents.
opts: True
False
why: Tool call and tool response intervention points apply to agents only. User input and output apply to models and agents.

q: A Foundry resource with public network access disabled needs token quotas enforced on model deployments through AI Gateway. What must be true of the API Management instance?
opts: It must be in a v2 tier and privately reachable, such as Standard v2 or Premium v2 with a private endpoint
It must be placed in a different Entra tenant from the Foundry resource for isolation
It must be a Developer tier instance that is exposed through a public IP address
It must be a Consumption tier instance, which can live in any subscription
why: An existing instance for AI Gateway must be a v2 tier in the same tenant and subscription, and with public access disabled it must also be reachable privately, for example Standard v2 or Premium v2 with a private endpoint or a Premium v2 VNet-injected instance. The other options violate the tier, tenant or privacy requirements.

q: Contoso wants agents published in Microsoft 365 to be approved before anyone can use them, and ownerless agents to be cleaned up. Which role can govern this without being Global Administrator?
opts: Reports Reader
Security Reader
User Account Administrator
AI Administrator
why: AI Administrator can view the registry and approve, install, block and manage agents. Security Reader, Reports Reader and User Account Administrator have limited visibility but cannot change agent configurations.

q: Eighty support agents each need the same OAuth permission and group membership, with approval and a 90-day expiry. Which Entra capability is designed for this?
opts: A Conditional Access policy that grants the permission when conditions are met
Entitlement management access packages for agent identities
A permanent role assignment made to each agent identity one at a time in PIM
Consent granted by each agent's developer when the agent is first deployed
why: Access packages bundle group membership, directory roles and API permissions with approval and expiration, and can be assigned to agent identities at scale. PIM role assignment is for roles rather than API permissions and group bundles, developer consent bypasses governance, and Conditional Access controls token issuance, not grants.

q: A Copilot Studio agent's tool invocation contains instructions injected from a web page. Contoso wants the action blocked while it is happening and an alert raised in the Defender portal. What should be configured?
opts: A DLP policy on Teams chat that blocks sensitive information types
Defender real-time protection for Copilot Studio agents, with the Microsoft 365 connector connected
Azure Policy for Kubernetes applied to the cluster that hosts the agent
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for the maker who built the agent
why: Real-time protection scans tool invocations at runtime, blocks suspicious behavior or cross-prompt injection and raises alerts, and the Microsoft 365 connector makes the alerts and incidents appear in the portal. DLP on chat, Kubernetes policy and a maker's Conditional Access do not inspect agent tool calls.

q: A new Azure VM must be protected against bootkits and rootkits and have its boot integrity attested. Which feature set should be used?
opts: Encryption at host, so that temporary disks and caches are encrypted
A just-in-time access policy that limits when management ports are open
Azure Bastion for browser-based access to the machine
Trusted launch with Secure Boot and vTPM
why: Trusted launch provides Secure Boot, a virtual TPM and boot integrity monitoring for generation 2 VMs and is the default for new ones. Encryption at host protects data at rest, JIT limits management ports and Bastion provides remote access.

q: Contoso must ensure all Windows and Linux servers, including Arc-enabled ones, have a specific TLS setting, with drift automatically corrected. Which feature fits?
opts: Defender for Servers Plan 1 with Defender for Endpoint integration
Just-in-time VM access on the management ports of each server
Azure Machine Configuration in Apply and Autocorrect mode
Azure Policy with the Audit effect on the VM resource properties in the subscription
why: Machine Configuration configures guest operating system settings on Azure and Arc-enabled machines, and Apply and Autocorrect returns a drifted machine to the required state. An Audit effect only reports and cannot see guest settings, JIT controls ports and Plan 1 provides EDR.

q: Servers in a subscription include some where no agent can be installed. Contoso wants vulnerability, malware and secrets scanning of their disks. Which capability fits?
opts: Agentless scanning in Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender for Servers Plan 1 with Defender for Endpoint integration
File integrity monitoring, which needs an agent on every server
Adaptive network hardening recommendations for the network security groups
why: Agentless scanning in Plan 2 (or Defender CSPM) analyzes disk snapshots for vulnerabilities, malware and secrets without installing software. Plan 1 focuses on EDR, which needs the sensor, and the other options do not scan disks for these findings.

q: Contoso needs Azure Container Registry with private endpoints and customer-managed keys. Which step is required?
opts: Allow anonymous pull
Use the Premium SKU
Enable the admin user
Use the Basic SKU with a service endpoint
why: Private endpoints and customer-managed keys are Premium SKU features. The admin user and anonymous pull weaken security, and Basic does not support these features.

q: A Container Apps environment must only be reachable from inside Contoso's network, and the app must authenticate users with Microsoft Entra without custom code. What should be configured?
opts: An external environment with an IP allow-list only
A public environment with function keys
An internal environment with VNet integration, and built-in authentication with Microsoft Entra
A Basic ACR with admin credentials
why: An internal environment limits ingress to the VNet, and built-in authentication provides Entra sign-in without custom code. An external environment is internet-facing, function keys belong to Azure Functions, and ACR admin credentials are unrelated.

q: An HTTP-triggered Azure Function must only accept calls from authenticated Contoso users, and the admin must know who is calling. Which approach is correct?
opts: Turn on App Service authentication with Microsoft Entra ID and require authentication
Rely on the function key in the URL
Enable HTTPS only and nothing else
Set the authorization level to anonymous and hide the URL
why: Authentication through Entra ID identifies the caller and can be required for all requests. Function keys are shared secrets that do not identify a user, anonymous with a hidden URL is security by obscurity, and HTTPS only protects transport but not who may call.

q: A Logic App starts with an HTTP request trigger, and anyone who obtains the callback URL can invoke it. How can Contoso restrict calls to authenticated Entra callers?
opts: Configure OAuth authorization policies for the request trigger
Turn on run history retention
Rename the workflow to hide the URL
Add a delay action at the start
why: Request triggers can require OAuth with Microsoft Entra authorization policies, and IP restrictions can add a network gate. Renaming, run history and delay actions do not control who can call.

q: Contoso exposes a back-end API through API Management and wants every call to carry a valid Entra token, with abusive clients throttled. Which policies should be used?
opts: validate-jwt and rate-limit
log-to-eventhub and send-request
set-header and cache-lookup
mock-response and forward-request
why: validate-jwt enforces a valid token and rate-limit throttles clients. The other pairs handle headers and caching, mocking and forwarding or logging and calls, none of which enforce authentication or throttling.

q: Administrators need to record RDP and SSH sessions to Azure VMs that have no public IPs, for audit. Which Azure Bastion SKU should be deployed?
opts: Developer
Standard
Basic
Premium
why: The Premium SKU adds session recording and private-only deployment. Developer is a free single-VM option, and Basic and Standard are dedicated SKUs without session recording.

q: After assigning the PCI DSS standard to a subscription in the regulatory compliance dashboard, a team notices that the subscription's Secure Score did not change. What explains this?
opts: Secure Score refreshes only once per calendar quarter, so new standards do not appear until then
Secure Score ignores any subscription that does not have a paid Defender plan enabled
The standard must first be assigned at the management group before Secure Score can reflect it
Standards are assessed for compliance control by control, while Secure Score reflects weighted security recommendations
why: The dashboard evaluates the environment against the controls of a named standard, whereas Secure Score aggregates weighted security recommendations, so adding a standard changes compliance reporting without changing the score by itself. Score is recalculated continuously, it is available without paid plans, and a standard can be assigned at the subscription scope.

q: Contoso wants Defender for Cloud to assess its Azure SQL databases for misconfigurations and excessive permissions, and to alert on anomalous access such as SQL injection attempts. Which should you enable?
opts: Defender CSPM with agentless discovery turned on
Defender for Storage with malware scanning
The Defender plan for Azure SQL databases
Defender for Resource Manager
why: The Defender plan for SQL combines vulnerability assessment (misconfigurations and permissions) with advanced threat protection (anomalous access and injection alerts). Defender CSPM provides posture management and attack path analysis but not database threat detection, and Defender for Storage and Resource Manager protect different resource types.

q: Contoso's production VMs keep their public IPs, but management ports must stay closed by default. Admins must request RDP access for a specific source IP and a limited time, and each request must be logged. Which feature meets this?
opts: Azure Bastion deployed in the VNet, with the public IPs removed from the VMs
PIM for Azure resource roles, requiring approval to activate Virtual Machine Contributor
Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Cloud, with a request per access
An Azure Firewall DNAT rule that is enabled only during working hours
why: JIT VM access keeps management ports closed and opens them temporarily for the requested source IP and duration, with each request logged. Bastion removes the need for public IPs rather than opening ports for a time window, PIM controls whether someone holds a role, not whether a port is reachable, and a scheduled DNAT rule is open to everyone during its window and has no per-request approval or logging.

q: Defender for Cloud has learned which applications normally run on a group of production VMs and now alerts when a process outside that learned allowlist runs. Which feature is this?
opts: Just-in-time VM access
File integrity monitoring
Adaptive application controls
Azure machine configuration auditing
why: Adaptive application controls use machine learning to build an allowlist of known-good applications for a VM group and alert, or enforce, on anything outside it. File integrity monitoring tracks changes to files and registry keys rather than which applications execute, JIT controls management port exposure, and machine configuration audits OS settings against a baseline. Note that Microsoft has deprecated the Log Analytics agent-based version of adaptive application controls, so this is a legacy feature that older material and exam items may still reference.

q: An auditor asks whether the Azure resources in a subscription currently meet the technical controls of ISO 27001, evaluated automatically from their configuration. Which feature answers this?
opts: Secure Score, which tracks weighted security recommendations
A Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager assessment for ISO 27001
The regulatory compliance dashboard with ISO 27001 assigned
An Azure Policy initiative with no mapping to ISO 27001 controls
why: The regulatory compliance dashboard maps Azure resource configuration to the controls of a named standard and shows which automated assessments pass or fail. Secure Score is general best practice, and Compliance Manager scores the organization's policies, processes and Microsoft 365 controls rather than evaluating Azure resource configuration. An initiative with no control mapping cannot report against ISO 27001.

q: Contoso adds an AWS account and wants its resources to appear in Defender for Cloud recommendations and Secure Score, without first installing an agent on every EC2 instance. What should you do?
opts: Install Azure Arc on every EC2 instance before AWS resources can appear in recommendations
Create an Azure Policy initiative whose scope is the AWS account's regions
Export AWS Security Hub findings into Microsoft Sentinel through a data connector
Onboard the AWS account with Defender for Cloud's native AWS connector
why: The native connector evaluates AWS resources agentlessly and feeds recommendations and Secure Score alongside Azure. Arc agents matter for server-level protection, not for posture recommendations on cloud resources. Azure Policy cannot target another cloud's accounts, and a Security Hub feed into Sentinel adds alerts to the SIEM without producing Defender for Cloud recommendations or score.

q: A SOC wants a Sentinel analytics rule, when it fires, to disable the user's Entra account automatically without a person taking action. What should you build?
opts: A playbook that analysts start manually from the incident page after review
A scheduled hunting query that adds a bookmark for an analyst to review
An automation rule on the analytics rule that runs a disable-user playbook
An Azure Monitor alert rule with an action group that emails the SOC
why: An automation rule triggers on incidents from the analytics rule and runs a playbook (Logic App) that calls the identity action, so no human is involved. A playbook started by hand needs an analyst, and a hunting bookmark and an emailing action group only notify people. None of them takes the action automatically.

q: A Sentinel analyst sees an unusual sign-in location and, separately, an unusual resource deployment. Individually low severity, together they suggest a multi-stage attack. Which capability surfaces such combinations automatically, without anyone writing a correlation query?
opts: A near-real-time analytics rule on sign-ins
UEBA anomalies for the affected user
Threat intelligence matching analytics
Fusion correlation across data sources
why: Fusion uses machine learning to correlate multiple lower-fidelity signals from different sources into one higher-confidence incident. A near-real-time rule watches a single query, UEBA builds a per-entity behavioral baseline, and threat intelligence matching compares indicators with logs. Each is useful, but none correlates two unrelated alerts into one multi-stage incident on its own.

q: A threat report describes a new attacker technique. An analyst wants to search the last 90 days of logs for it and save suspicious results as evidence, although no alert exists. What should the analyst use?
opts: A scheduled analytics rule that runs every 5 minutes
A playbook that runs the query when an incident is created
A workbook that visualizes the table
Hunting queries, with bookmarks for the suspicious results
why: Hunting queries are manual, proactive searches over historical data, and bookmarks preserve interesting results that can later become an incident. A scheduled rule is forward-looking detection, a playbook is automation that runs after an incident exists, and a workbook visualizes data without saving evidence.

q: Contoso enables Microsoft Sentinel on a Log Analytics workspace that already collects Azure Activity Log and VM performance data. What happens to that existing data?
opts: Existing tables become available only after they are re-ingested through a Sentinel data connector
Sentinel copies the existing data into a Sentinel-managed store, which doubles ingestion for those tables
Sentinel can query the existing tables as soon as it is enabled, because it is built on Log Analytics
Sentinel can be enabled only on a new, empty workspace, so the data must be exported first
why: Sentinel has no separate data store; it operates on the Log Analytics workspace, so tables already there are immediately available to analytics rules and hunting. Nothing needs to be re-ingested, copied or exported, and an existing workspace can be used.

q: Twenty alert rules notify the same on-call list. Contoso wants recipients changed in one place and notifications suppressed during a planned maintenance window without editing the alert rules. What should you use?
opts: A separate action group per alert rule, tagged for maintenance
An automation rule in Sentinel that closes the incidents during the window
The mute actions setting on each alert rule for the length of the window
A shared action group plus an alert processing rule for the maintenance window
why: One action group referenced by every rule centralizes recipients, and an alert processing rule can suppress actions for a schedule across many rules without touching them. Separate action groups multiply the places to edit, a Sentinel automation rule works on Sentinel incidents rather than Azure Monitor alerts, and muting each rule individually means editing every rule.

q: A subscription that passes every automated assessment in its PCI DSS standard on the regulatory compliance dashboard must also have a Secure Score of 100 percent.
opts: True
False
why: The two measure different things: the standard covers the controls mapped to PCI DSS, while Secure Score aggregates weighted recommendations across best-practice security controls. Passing one does not imply the other, and neither is a formal certification.

q: Just-in-time VM access works by adding a temporary allow rule for an approved source IP, port and time window to the VM's NSG or Azure Firewall, rather than by closing the port inside the guest operating system.
opts: True
False
why: JIT is a network-layer control that manages rules for the VM's NSG or firewall. The port is blocked by default through those rules, and approved requests add short-lived exceptions that are removed when the window ends.

q: A scheduled Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule can query tables in more than one Log Analytics workspace by using cross-workspace queries.
opts: True
False
why: Analytics rules support cross-workspace queries, so a single rule can correlate data held in several workspaces. It sounds contradictory to the idea that Sentinel lives in one workspace, but the rule can reference others.

q: A Sentinel playbook that uses the incident trigger runs automatically whenever an incident is created, without an automation rule or manual action.
opts: True
False
why: A playbook has to be invoked. An automation rule that runs the playbook is what makes it run automatically on incident creation, and otherwise an analyst starts it manually from the incident.

q: After an AWS account is onboarded through Defender for Cloud's native connector, its resources are assessed against a built-in AWS security standard and findings appear alongside Azure findings in recommendations and Secure Score.
opts: True
False
why: The native multicloud connector assigns a default AWS security standard and surfaces the results in the same recommendations and score view as Azure resources.

q: Contoso wants workload protection for VMs, storage accounts and SQL databases in one subscription. Which two statements about Defender for Cloud plans are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Enabling Defender for Storage also turns on vulnerability assessment for SQL databases
Plans are enabled per resource type, so enabling the servers plan does not protect storage accounts
Secure Score and recommendations appear only after a paid plan is enabled
Plans can be enabled only at the management group level
Foundational posture management with recommendations remains available without any paid plan
why: Each plan covers its own resource type and must be enabled separately, while foundational posture management (recommendations and Secure Score) is available without a paid plan. Enabling one plan does not enable another, and plans are configured per subscription.

q: Contoso's SOC wants to detect multi-stage attacks that span identity and Azure resource activity. Which two statements about Microsoft Sentinel Fusion are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Fusion needs an analyst to write a correlation query for each attack scenario
Fusion uses machine learning to combine low-fidelity signals into one incident
Fusion works only when every signal comes from one data connector
Fusion can detect multi-stage patterns that single-source rules do not flag
Fusion removes the need to connect data sources to the workspace
why: Fusion correlates alerts and signals across data sources automatically, which is what lets it spot multi-stage attacks that single-source rules treat as unrelated. It does not need hand-written correlation queries, it is not limited to one connector, and it still depends on connected data sources.

q: A security team wants to see the specific chain of exploitable resources and misconfigurations -- such as an internet-exposed VM with a known vulnerability that can reach a database holding sensitive data -- that an attacker could actually follow to compromise a business-critical asset. Which Defender for Cloud capability shows this?
opts: Secure Score, aggregated across every recommendation in the subscription
The regulatory compliance dashboard, mapped against a named standard like ISO 27001
Attack path analysis, built on the cloud security graph
Just-in-time VM access, temporarily opening a single management port for one approved requester
why: Attack path analysis, built on the cloud security graph, visualizes the specific exploitable chains across resources that an attacker could actually follow to reach a business-critical asset, prioritizing what is genuinely reachable and exploitable rather than presenting a flat list of recommendations. Secure Score is an aggregate percentage, the compliance dashboard maps against a named standard, and JIT access only controls temporary port exposure -- none of them trace a multi-resource exploitation chain the way attack path analysis does.

q: Contoso's security lead plans governance rules in Defender for Cloud. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A governance rule can assign an owner and a remediation due date to matching recommendations
Governance rules apply the recommended fix automatically when the due date passes
Governance rules can be created only for Key Vault recommendations
Owners can be notified about overdue assignments, giving the rule an escalation path
Governance rules change a recommendation's weight in Secure Score
why: Governance rules drive accountability by assigning owners and due dates and notifying about overdue items. They do not remediate anything themselves, they are not tied to one resource type, and they do not alter Secure Score weighting.

q: A security team has two different needs: leadership wants a single trending number reflecting overall best-practice posture quarter over quarter, while the SOC wants to see the exact chain of exploitable resources an attacker could follow right now to reach the customer database. Which Defender for Cloud capability addresses each need, respectively?
opts: Secure Score for the trend metric; attack path analysis for the exploitable chain
Attack path analysis for the trend metric; Secure Score for the exploitable chain
The regulatory compliance dashboard for both needs, since it covers trend and exploitability together
Secure Score for both needs, since a higher score always means fewer exploitable paths
why: Secure Score is the aggregate, weighted best-practice trend metric leadership wants, while attack path analysis (built on the cloud security graph) traces the specific exploitable, reachable chain the SOC is asking about -- swapping those two would misapply each tool. The compliance dashboard maps posture against a named standard rather than doing either job, and a higher Secure Score does not guarantee fewer exploitable paths, since score and reachability are measuring different things.

q: A security architect explains how just-in-time VM access and Azure Bastion each reduce RDP and SSH exposure. Which statement is accurate?
opts: Bastion needs a public IP on each target VM, and JIT is the feature that removes those addresses
JIT adds temporary allow rules on the VM's existing address, while Bastion needs no public IP on the VM
JIT can open a port only after Azure Bastion has been deployed in the same virtual network
Bastion rewrites the VM subnet's NSG rules for each session and removes them when it ends
why: JIT keeps ports closed and opens them for an approved requester, source and time on the VM's existing address, while Bastion proxies sessions over TLS to private IPs, so the VM needs no public address. They are independent features, and Bastion relies on a standing NSG allowance from its own subnet rather than rewriting rules per session.

q: Contoso's SOC reviews attack path analysis in Defender for Cloud. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: It models relationships between resources, exposures and vulnerabilities on the cloud security graph
It lists each recommendation in isolation, ordered by Secure Score weight
It automatically removes the exposure at the first resource in each path
It prioritizes paths by whether an attacker could reach a business-critical asset
It is evaluated only against a named regulatory standard such as ISO 27001
why: Attack path analysis chains exposures and vulnerabilities across resources on the cloud security graph and prioritizes the chains that reach critical assets. It is not an isolated recommendation list, it does not remediate anything itself, and it is not tied to a regulatory standard.

q: A Defender for Cloud recommendation goes unaddressed because nobody feels responsible. The security lead wants an owner and a fix-by date attached, with an escalation if the date passes. Which feature should you configure?
opts: Workflow automation that runs a Logic App when the recommendation is generated
An Azure Policy exemption on the recommendation that expires after 30 days
A governance rule that assigns an owner and a due date, with escalation for overdue items
Email notifications to the subscription owner for high-severity recommendations
why: Governance rules attach an owner and a remediation timeframe to recommendations and track or escalate overdue items. Workflow automation reacts to a recommendation by running an action but assigns no accountability, an exemption removes the recommendation from view, and a notification email does not give any specific person an owned deadline.

q: A user who signs in only during business hours from one city accesses several permitted resources at 3 a.m. from a new location. No known attack signature matches, but the team wants it flagged as unusual for that user. Which Sentinel capability does this?
opts: A scheduled analytics rule that matches a known attack pattern
Threat intelligence matching analytics
User and Entity Behavior Analytics
Fusion correlation across low-severity alerts
why: UEBA builds a behavioral baseline for each user and entity and flags deviations from that individual's normal activity, which fits permitted-but-unusual behavior. A scheduled rule needs a known pattern, threat intelligence matching needs a known-bad indicator, and Fusion correlates separate alerts rather than one person's baseline.

q: A Sentinel analytics rule that references a watchlist through the _GetWatchlist function sees changes to the watchlist without the rule's query being edited.
opts: True
False
why: Watchlists are named, centrally maintained lookup tables. Rules and hunting queries reference them by alias, so updating the watchlist updates every query that uses it.

q: Contoso's SOC wants abnormal-behavior detection and clear remediation ownership. Which two statements about Sentinel UEBA and Defender for Cloud governance rules are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: UEBA flags deviations from an entity's own baseline without a signature
UEBA detects an anomaly only after analysts author a rule for that specific pattern
A governance rule applies the fix once an owner has been assigned to it
UEBA covers only Azure virtual machines and nothing else in the tenant
A governance rule assigns an owner and a due date to a recommendation
why: UEBA's value is baselining each user or entity and flagging deviations without a predefined signature, and governance rules attach owners and due dates to recommendations. UEBA does not need a hand-written rule per pattern, it covers users and other entities rather than only VMs, and governance rules track remediation rather than performing it.

q: An executive dashboard shows three different percentages for the same organization: one from Defender for Cloud reflecting infrastructure best-practice posture, one mapped specifically to ISO 27001, and one from Microsoft Purview reflecting data governance and documented policy controls across Microsoft 365 and Azure. Which pairing correctly matches each percentage to its source?
opts: Secure Score (ISO 27001 mapping), the regulatory compliance dashboard (infrastructure best practice), and Purview Compliance Manager's compliance score (data governance and policy controls)
Secure Score (infrastructure best practice), the regulatory compliance dashboard (ISO 27001 mapping), and Purview Compliance Manager's compliance score (data governance and policy controls)
All three percentages come from the same Secure Score calculation, just displayed with different filters applied
Purview Compliance Manager's compliance score covers infrastructure best practice, while Secure Score covers data governance and policy controls
why: Secure Score is Defender for Cloud's general infrastructure best-practice metric, the regulatory compliance dashboard maps that same infrastructure posture against a specific named standard like ISO 27001, and Purview Compliance Manager's compliance score separately covers data governance and documented policy controls. The other options either swap which tool covers which scope or incorrectly claim all three come from one calculation.

q: Contoso keeps Sentinel logs for two years to meet audit requirements, with the first 90 days in interactive retention and the remainder in archive. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Interactive retention keeps data immediately queryable by analytics rules and hunting queries
A scheduled analytics rule can query archived data directly with no additional step
Archived data needs a search job or a restore before it can be queried like active data
Interactive and archive retention periods cannot both be configured for the same table
why: Interactive retention is what keeps data immediately queryable by analytics rules, hunting queries and workbooks, while archived data has to go through a search job or be restored to interactive retention before it can be queried the same way. A scheduled analytics rule cannot query archived data directly, and a single table can have both an interactive and an archive retention period.

q: Contoso's Security Copilot users in a non-E5 tenant get requests rejected during peak incident hours, although their capacity is provisioned. What should be added so peaks are absorbed without hourly provisioning?
opts: Contributor access for all analysts
More Security Copilot owners
A second Log Analytics workspace
Overage SCUs, with a maximum limit or unlimited
why: Overage capacity is consumed as used when provisioned SCUs are depleted and can be capped or unlimited. More owners, another workspace and more contributor rights do not add compute capacity.

q: An analyst holds the Security Copilot contributor role but cannot retrieve any Sentinel incidents in prompts. Which two statements explain it? (Choose two.)
opts: The contributor role is a Microsoft Entra role that automatically includes Sentinel access
Plugins use on-behalf-of authentication, so the analyst also needs a Sentinel role such as Reader
Security Copilot roles grant platform access only, not security data
Sentinel data is never available to Security Copilot
why: Security Copilot owner and contributor roles are platform roles, not Entra roles, and plugins act on behalf of the user, so the user needs the permissions in the underlying product. The role does not carry Sentinel access, and Sentinel data is available through the plugin when the user has rights.

q: Which statement about Security Copilot capacity for Microsoft 365 E5 customers is correct?
opts: They must provision a minimum of 10 SCUs per hour before use
Capacity cannot be monitored
Eligible tenants are auto-provisioned with a default capacity
SCUs are billed per user per month
why: Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers receive an automatically provisioned default capacity. SCUs are a compute unit billed as provisioned capacity or overage, not per user, the minimum for provisioning is one SCU, and usage can be monitored.

q: Who should be able to publish a custom plugin for everyone in the Security Copilot workspace?
opts: Anyone with Reader on the subscription
Only the people the owners explicitly allow, which can be owners only
Only Microsoft
Every user in the tenant by default
why: Owners control whether contributors can add and manage custom plugins at user or organization scope. By default only owners do. Tenant users and subscription Readers have no such right.

q: Contoso starts a new Sentinel deployment in 2026. Which statement should guide the design?
opts: Use only the Azure portal because the Defender portal does not support Sentinel without XDR
Plan for the Microsoft Defender portal, because Sentinel in the Azure portal is not supported after March 31, 2027
Use the Defender portal only if Microsoft 365 E5 is purchased
Wait until 2028 for the Defender portal to be available
why: Sentinel is generally available in the Defender portal, including for customers without Defender XDR or E5, and the Azure portal experience ends on March 31, 2027. The other statements are incorrect.

q: A playbook-based automation rule is not triggering the Logic App. The playbook is in a resource group. Which is the most likely missing permission?
opts: Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group
Global Reader for the analyst
Playbook Operator for Sentinel's service account
Reader on the subscription
why: Sentinel needs the Automation Contributor role on the resource group of the playbook to run it from an automation rule. Playbook Operator is for people running playbooks manually, and Global Reader and subscription Reader do not grant that permission.

q: Contoso wants SOC staff to create analytics rules and install solutions from the content hub, but not manage Azure RBAC. Which role fits?
opts: Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
Microsoft Sentinel Responder
Microsoft Sentinel Reader
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
why: Contributor can create and edit rules and manage the content hub. Responder manages incidents, Reader is view-only and Playbook Operator only runs playbooks.

q: A firewall appliance cannot run an agent and sends CEF messages. Which design collects them in Sentinel?
opts: Send the logs to a Key Vault
Install the Log Analytics agent on the firewall
Send to a Linux forwarder with Azure Monitor Agent and the Common Event Format via AMA connector
Enable diagnostic settings on the firewall appliance
why: Appliances send Syslog or CEF to a Linux forwarder running Azure Monitor Agent, which uses a data collection rule and the connector to forward to the workspace. The legacy Log Analytics agent cannot be installed on the appliance, Key Vault is not a log destination, and diagnostic settings apply to Azure resources.

q: Contoso reduces Windows Security event ingestion cost by collecting only specific event IDs from servers, some of which are on-premises. Which approach is right?
opts: Collect all events and delete rows later
Windows Security Events via AMA with a DCR filter and Azure Arc
Use Syslog via AMA
Install the legacy Microsoft Monitoring Agent
why: The AMA-based connector uses a DCR to filter events at the source, and non-Azure machines need Azure Arc first. The legacy agent is retired, collecting everything defeats cost control, and Syslog is for Linux sources.

q: After deploying Windows Event Forwarding to a WEC server running Azure Monitor Agent, built-in Windows Security analytics rules stop matching. Why?
opts: The WEC server needs a Log Analytics agent instead
The rules only work on Linux
Windows Event Forwarding is not supported by Sentinel
Forwarded events are written to the WindowsEvent table, not SecurityEvent
why: Windows Forwarded Events land in WindowsEvent, but many built-in rules query SecurityEvent; rules must be adapted or the Windows Security Events connector used. WEF is supported, rules are not Linux-only, and the agent is AMA.

q: A vendor system posts JSON logs to Azure by REST API, and Contoso needs them in a table with only some fields kept. What should be used?
opts: A custom table, the Logs Ingestion API and a DCR transformation
A Network Watcher packet capture
The Syslog connector
A Key Vault secret per log
why: The Logs Ingestion API sends JSON to a DCR, which can transform and filter the data into a custom table. The Syslog connector, Key Vault and packet captures do not ingest custom REST data.

q: Verbose firewall and storage access logs cost too much in the Sentinel analytics tier and are rarely used. Which approach is right?
opts: Delete them after 24 hours
Keep everything in the analytics tier for two years
Export to a spreadsheet
Store them in the data lake tier and summarize with KQL jobs when needed
why: Secondary, high-volume data belongs in the data lake tier, with KQL jobs summarizing results into the analytics tier. Deleting them loses investigation value, analytics tier for all data is costly, and spreadsheets do not scale.

q: The analytics tier in Microsoft Sentinel keeps data in interactive retention for 90 days by default and can extend it to two years.
opts: True
False
why: The analytics tier has 90 days of interactive retention by default and can be extended up to two years; data kept longer overall remains available in the data lake tier.

q: An investigator needs to find who isolated a device and who changed a Defender security role last week. Where is this recorded?
opts: In Sentinel hunting queries only
In NSG flow logs
In the audit log that Microsoft Defender reads from Microsoft Purview auditing
In Azure Activity logs
why: Defender XDR and Defender for Endpoint activities are audited and visible through Purview auditing, requiring auditing to be on and the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role. Hunting queries find attacker activity, and Azure Activity and flow logs record other planes.

q: Which Defender for Cloud plan provides outside-in discovery of internet-facing resources without a separate EASM license?
opts: Defender CSPM
Defender for Storage
Defender for Servers Plan 1 with Defender for Endpoint integration
Defender for Key Vault
why: The Defender External Attack Surface Management integration is included with Defender CSPM. The other plans protect their own resources and do not run outside-in scans.

q: A new Windows VM was built with Defender for Servers Plan 2 enabled. Contoso wants the vulnerability assessment source to be the integrated Microsoft solution. What is the default?
opts: Manual scans with PowerShell
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
A third-party scanner that must be licensed first
Azure Backup
why: Defender for Servers includes Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management as the vulnerability assessment solution, with premium capabilities in Plan 2. Third-party scanners are optional, and PowerShell and Backup are not vulnerability scanners.
